Inspectors general often conduct informal inquiries into complaints against staffers and many times those inquiries do not result in a full-on investigation, which can result in disciplinary action up to and including dismissal.The state department has declined to comment on a potential IG investigation.The top two Democrats on the House foreign affairs and Senate foreign relations committees, Representative Gregory Meeks of New York and Senator Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, as well as the ranking member on the House committee for oversight and government reform, Robert Garcia, Democrat of California, have already called for an investigation into Guilfoyle.Since late September, the Journal has detailed numerous accounts of questionable conduct by Guilfoyle. Its first report said that she had told guests at a reception that the US could undermine the Greek government if it chose to, promoted the business interests of one particular Greek construction and energy company, and allowed its lobbyist into private diplomatic meetings.While Rubio was in Athens, the Journal reported – citing text messages – that Guilfoyle had asked a Trump donor and supporter to pay a $100,000 credit card bill just before her confirmation hearing, promising him access to administration officials if he did.The Journal then reported that Guilfoyle had been enraged about not being invited to a Greek-themed event at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, earlier this year and demanded to attend while boasting about luxury travel to France with energy company executives.Another report, from the British tabloid The Daily Mail, said that Guilfoyle had alienated staff at the US embassy in Athens and had pushed the bounds of behavior appropriate for the top representative of the US government to Greece.Guilfoyle is a former Fox News Channel host and California prosecutor who was once engaged to Trump’s son Donald Jr.Explore more on these topicsTrump administrationUS politicsDonald TrumpMarco RubioUS foreign policynewsShareReuse this content

title: Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats must ‘win by massive numbers’ to fend off Trump election denial | US midterm elections 2026 | The Guardian
description: Democratic Senate candidate’s remarks come as Trump has long baselessly claimed his 2020 election loss was stolen
Author: Eric Berger
Headline: Democratic Senate candidate’s remarks come as Trump has long baselessly claimed his 2020 election loss was stolen
Content: Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during a campaign town hall at Cadillac high school on Saturday in Cadillac, Michigan.Photograph: Chip Somodevilla/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDemocratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during a campaign town hall at Cadillac high school on Saturday in Cadillac, Michigan.Photograph: Chip Somodevilla/Getty ImagesUS midterm elections 2026Abdul El-Sayed: Democrats must ‘win by massive numbers’ to fend off Trump election denialDemocratic Senate candidate’s remarks come as Trump has long baselessly claimed his 2020 election loss was stolenEric BergerSun 11 Oct 2026 13.23 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 13.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDemocratsmust “win by massive numbers” during November’s federal midterm elections becauseDonald Trumpand his Republican allies are bound to try to sow doubt about the integrity of the results, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan said on Sunday.El-Sayed’s comments on NBC’s Meet the Press came with the Democratsfavored to wincontrol of the House of Representatives during the 3 November midterms – and polls show that the party could also win Senate seats in states that traditionally elect Republicans and gain a majority there, too.Meanwhile, Trump has long baselessly maintained that the 2020 presidential election which he lost as an incumbent to Joe Biden was stolen by fraudsters.He also gave a primetime speech in July in which he made unverified claims aboutChinese interferencein the election, and hefired membersof an independent federal election commission.When asked later by a rightwing broadcaster whether the president might declare anational security emergencypertaining to elections for the midterms, Trump ignited alarm among some observers by replying: “Let me just say, stranger things have happened, OK?”The New York Times, meanwhile, reported that Trump had cast doubt on electionson 440 daysof his second presidency, which began in early 2025.As such, on NBC’s Meet the Press Sunday, El-Sayedwas askedwhether Democrats needed to turn out in such numbers in November that the election would be “too big to rig” – as it had recently been put by former vice-president Kamala Harris, who lost the 2024 White House election to Trump.“Donald Trump has already threatened to do what he did in 2020, which is deny the outcomes of an election,” El-Sayed said. “So, yes, we have to win by massive numbers.”The Cook Political Reportrevised its predictionson Tuesday and declared that “A Senate Majority is Squarely in Democrats’ Sights”.A recent New York Times and Siena University poll found Democratic Senate candidates leading inAlaska, Ohio and Texas, states that Trump won by double digits in 2024.The poll showed El-Sayed leading Republican candidate Mike Rogers by five points.El-Sayed on Sunday’s Meet the Press alluded to how Rogers had also claimed that a 2024US Senateelection which he lost to Elissa Slotkin, a Democrat, was stolen from him – after first having conceded the race.Rogers in November 2025 wasreportedto have said at events that a single van carrying fraudulent ballots in Detroit cost him the race against Slotkin.“The guy … I’m running against insinuates that he didn’t actually lose,” El-Sayed said to Kristen Welker. “That’s the guy I’m running against right now.”Explore more on these topicsUS midterm elections 2026DemocratsDonald TrumpUS politicsMichiganUS SenateHouse of RepresentativesnewsShareReuse this content

title: ICE agent strikes man with vehicle during pursuit in Texas, officials say | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) | The Guardian
description: Parra-Hernandez suffered a broken leg and taken to a hospital after being hit by car during an ICE operation
Author: Eric Berger
Headline: Parra-Hernandez suffered a broken leg and taken to a hospital after being hit by car during an ICE operation
Content: A rally against ICE in New York City on Saturday after agents shot and wounded a man in the Marble Hill neighborhood on 8 October.Photograph: Olga Fedorova/EPAView image in fullscreenA rally against ICE in New York City on Saturday after agents shot and wounded a man in the Marble Hill neighborhood on 8 October.Photograph: Olga Fedorova/EPAICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement)ICE agent strikes man with vehicle during pursuit in Texas, officials sayParra-Hernandez suffered a broken leg and taken to a hospital after being hit by car during an ICE operationEric BergerSun 11 Oct 2026 10.54 EDTFirst published on Sun 11 Oct 2026 10.13 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAn Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent driving a vehicle struck a man on Saturday while trying to pursue him and someone else in the Houston area, according to authorities.The federal agency had been trying to pull over and arrest Jose Mendoza-Cervantes in north-west Harris county,Texas, when he and the victim, Miguel Parra-Hernandez, exited the vehicle, officials said.Surveillance footage showed the officer chase Parra-Hernandez and then hit him with his car. Parra-Hernandez suffered a broken leg and was taken to a hospital, theHarris county sheriff’s officesaid.In a statement, the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) that oversees ICE said the agency had been trying to arrest Mendoza-Cervantes after a judge had issued him a final order of removal from the United States.Mendoza-Cervantes had been arrested four times for driving under the influence and arrested for unlawful possession of a firearm, the DHS statement added. He remained at large as of Saturday morning.DHS did not address questions from the Guardian seeking the name of the officer who struck Parra-Hernandez and whether he was equipped with a body-worn camera, which ICE policy requires.‘Deeply concerning’: Democratic congressional candidate rebukes ICE’s presence in New YorkRead moreParra-Hernandez’s hospitalization came with ICE facingcriticismthroughout Donald Trump’s second presidency for the agency’saggressive arrest, detention and deportation tactics.More than 30 people have died in 2026 during interactions with immigration officials, the Guardian reported in late September.On Friday morning, a 72-year-old man shot an off-duty ICE official who was “intoxicated and agitated” and was accused of attacking the man and his daughter on their property in Fresno, California.On Thursday, in New York City, an ICE agentshot a manwho was in his vehicle with a five-year-old child, mayor Zohran Mamdani said ina statement.Markwayne Mullin, the Trump administration’s homeland security secretary, later said on CBS’s Face the Nation that ICE took the time to learn the “pattern of life” of the man shot in New York on Thursday – but “we didn’t know the five-year-old was in the vehicle”.The Harris county precinct 4 commissioner, Lesley Briones, alluded tothose various other casesin a statementon Saturday, saying: “Under the Trump administration, ICE has brought chaos and destruction to communities across our country.”Briones described herself as “horrified” after Parra-Hernandez’s case on Saturday and called for ICE to release any relevant video to the sheriff’s office.DHS did not immediately respond to the Guardian when asked for comment on Sunday.Explore more on these topicsICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement)US immigrationHoustonTexasTrump administrationUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: US’s Reagan-era economic promises return as Trump’s AI-fueled growth fantasy | US economy | The Guardian
description: ‘Even if AI supercharged the economy, its impact on the government’s finances would be muted’
Author: Eduardo Porter
Headline: ‘Even if AI supercharged the economy, its impact on the government’s finances would be muted’
Content: Donald Trump and the Meta CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, listen as Dario Amodei speaks to reporters at the White House on 29 September, after meeting with top executives of AI firms.Photograph: Alex Brandon/APView image in fullscreenDonald Trump and the Meta CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, listen as Dario Amodei speaks to reporters at the White House on 29 September, after meeting with top executives of AI firms.Photograph: Alex Brandon/APUS economyAnalysisUS’s Reagan-era economic promises return as Trump’s AI-fueled growth fantasyEduardo Porter‘Even if AI supercharged the economy, its impact on the government’s finances would be muted’Sun 11 Oct 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 07.02 EDTShareBack through political history to the age ofRonald Reagan, Republicans have repeatedly promised the US public that tax cuts would pay for themselves, firing up economic growth and filling the government’s coffers.The promise never really panned out. From the Gipper’s day on, the Republicans’ tax cuts inevitably increased the budget deficit. Despite its failure, though, the promise is back, coated in a fine new layer ofartificial intelligencepixie dust. It will fail again.The treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, is relying on an AI-laced economy when he promises to deliver annual economic growth of 3% – a rate that, except for the rebound from the Covid pandemic, has been achievedonly twicethis century. Dreams of AI inflect Donald Trump’s fantasy that “we’re growing at a faster rate than we’ve ever grown before,” which will allow the government to “take care of the40 trillion” in federal debt “over a period of time”.Financial markets, however, are not buying. Last week, the yield on the10-year treasury bondsurged to its highest in almost a quarter century, more than a full percentage point higher than when Trump launched his misbegotten war against Iran.Line chart showing a recent upward trend in 10-year US treasury bond yieldsThe war’s inflationary impact is the most immediate cause of rising bond yields. It already persuaded the Fed to raise short-term interest rates. But the treasury market is alsobeing wallopedby the US’s unbalanced finances. There is no realistic path for economic growth to generate the tax revenues needed to fix the US’s enormous and growing budget deficit. Investors are demanding more to cover the growing funding gap.Borrowing is likely to become more expensive still. Foreign central banks, which once reliably bought treasuries to build up foreign reserves and manage their exchange rates,have cut backon their exposure to US government debt. The treasury now relies largely on private investors seeking to turn a profit. It finds itself competing for their money with the very AI superscalers on which it is pinning its future hopes, which are borrowing hand over fist to fund the buildout of datacenters to train their agents.Indeed, the US’s finances find themselves in a bit of a negative spiral, as rising bond yields put additional pressure on the budget. Interest payments on the federal debt alone are consuming 3.3% of GDP, up from an average of 2.1% over the preceding 50 years.And Trump’s fiscal management – his One Big Beautiful Bill Act is estimated toadd $4.7tnto the federal debt through 2035 – is not making the budget math easier. The deficit already hit 6% of GDP – twice the size Bessent once promised.The Congressional Budget Office projectedit will close in on 7% of GDP by 2033. And that was before Trump promised a $5,000 “dividend” to every US adult if the GOP kept control of Congress in the midterms. There is no realistic amount of growth that can fill the fiscal hole that Trump keeps digging.The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFPB)sketched out a few scenarios. Assuming the temporary tax cuts in Trump’s 2025 law are made permanent by a future Congress – an assumption that fits the historical pattern – and that the government does not recover the revenue lost when the supreme court struck down its national security tariffs, achieving a budget deficit of 3% of GDP by 2036 would require annual growth of 4.4% over the next decade. Achieving a balanced budget by then would require the economy to expand 7.2% per year.It is not impossible for AI to deliver this kind of growth. Some economists are willing tocontemplate scenariosin which artificial intelligence boosts economic growth to 15% per year, by taking over much of the cognitive work usually performed by humans. But these scenarios do not appear likely.According to the CFRB, stabilizing the federal debt would require average growth in total factor productivity – a measure of how efficiently economic inputs are converted into goods and services – to hit 2.5% per year over the next decade. The US hasonly hit thatonce since 1959. And that is despite massive productivity gains over the period from electrification, the completion of the federal highway system, the telecommunications revolution and the first wave of IT and automation.Even if AI supercharged the economy, its impact on the government’s finances would be muted, for it would massively shift the fruits of growth from labor to capital, and the tax rate on capital today is only about half the tax rate on labor. Moreover, such a shift in the distribution of economic spoils would probably call formassive government spendingto sustain the livelihoods of the many workers left behind.What can we expect from the AI-pixie dust? At the moment people seem particularly worried about AI agents slipping their enclosures and killing us all. But even short of that, it is not a given that their impact will be inevitably positive for the economy, not to say the government’s finances necessarily provide the money for the federal government to right its finances.For one, their massive debt-fuelled investments are pushing interest rates higher, complicating government financing. Their future promise, moreover, also comes with momentous risk.The Stanford economistHanno Lustig estimatesthat for the owners of datacenters to break even on their massive investments in AI – estimated to reach $1.43tn this year – their revenue would have to grow by 45% on average every year for the next seven years. By 2032, it would amount to roughly 9.2% of GDP.Asimilar analysisby Jared Bernstein, former chair of Joe Biden’s Council of Economic Advisers, and Stanford economist Ryan Cummings, concluded that the nation’s six superscalers – Google, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, SpaceX and Amazon – would need additional revenues of $13.1tn to $18.7tn over the next 10 years just to pay for their massive investments in AI. That is roughly the same as their total revenues over the last 10 years.It’s hard to forecast precisely what would happen to financial markets were these targets to be missed. But it’s safe to say that it might complicate the task of trimming the budget deficit and financing the US’s vast public debt.Eduardo Porter is a journalist focused on economics and politics. He writes the newsletterBeing Thereon SubstackExplore more on these topicsUS economyEconomicsAI (artificial intelligence)US politicsanalysisShareReuse this content

title: ‘Some aren’t going to make it’: how pressure on farmers threatens UK food security | UK news | The Guardian
description: Food producers are adding their voices to the chorus of warnings about the vulnerability of British supply chains
Author: Joanna Partridge
Headline: Food producers are adding their voices to the chorus of warnings about the vulnerability of British supply chains
Content: Jamie Burrows, the chair of the crops board at the National Farmers’ Union, says there are multiple challenges facing him and other food producers.Photograph: National Farmers' UnionView image in fullscreenJamie Burrows, the chair of the crops board at the National Farmers’ Union, says there are multiple challenges facing him and other food producers.Photograph: National Farmers' UnionUK news‘Some aren’t going to make it’: how pressure on farmers threatens UK food securityFood producers are adding their voices to the chorus of warnings about the vulnerability of British supply chainsJoanna PartridgeSun 11 Oct 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 10.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“There are so many decent, capable, productive, efficient arable farmers out there, asking how they are supposed to finance the crop they are meant to be putting in the ground,” Jamie Burrows says.Sitting in his tractor at his arable farm in Norfolk, Burrows is listing the multiple challenges facing him and other food producers.Crop growers such as Burrows are ploughing and cultivating their fields, preparing the ground – hardened and dried out during the long, hot summer – for their next crop.But machinery requires fuel, and the cost of red diesel – used for agricultural vehicles and machinery that is taxed at a lower rate than standard diesel –has almost doubledsince theconflict in Iranbegan in late February. The cost of most fertilisers used to grow crops and feed for animals has also soared by about 20% over the same period.British government ‘complacent about food as a national security matter’Read more“Some of these businesses aren’t going to make it,” concludes Burrows, who is also the chair of the crops board at the National Farmers’ Union (NFU). “It is very, very difficult.”These are among the latest worries for Britain’s food producers, who also faced a succession of heatwaves and drought conditions during theUK’s hottest summer on record, which resulted in England’s worst recorded cereals harvest, according toofficial production estimates.Farmers, the first link in the food production chain, are adding their voices to the chorus of warnings about the vulnerability and precarity of the UK’s food supply.Food experts, academics, businesses and thepublic spending watchdog, the National Audit Office (NAO), have in recent weeks called on the government to work on making the UK’s food system more resilient.The climate crisis, this year’shuge El Niño weather pattern, geopolitical shocks, energy outages and cyber-attacks areall considered threatsto food chain security.View image in fullscreenFarmers are adding their voices to the chorus of warnings about the vulnerability and precarity of the UK’s food supply.Photograph: Christopher Furlong/Getty ImagesAmid calls for ministers to treat food as a national security issue, parliament’s influential public accounts committee is to begin a series of hearings on Monday as part of its inquiry into the resilience of the UK’s food supply.MPs on the committee will look at the NAO’s findings on the shortcomings of the last catastrophe planning exercise by the Department for Environment,Foodand Rural Affairs (Defra), which largely excluded food supply chain businesses.Britain produces about 60% of the food it needs to feed itself, but is more dependent on imports than many European peers. The government’s own research has shown Britons are less prepared for potential future emergencies than several European neighbours.Some in the food industry believe there are signs Andy Burnham’s government is beginning to take the threats to Britain’s food system more seriously.The Cabinet Office will launch a campaign telling households to stock up on tinned foods alongside preparations for possible future emergencies. The government’sPreparewebsite outlines steps it says people should take, which include storing items at home, including bottles of water and nonperishable food, such as tinned meat, fruit and vegetables that do not require cooking.Britons kept in dark about scale of climate crisis, say viewers of ‘first-of-its-kind’ emergency briefingRead moreDespite this,a recent warningfrom more than 150 food experts and academics accused ministers of being “complacent” about food security and not having a plan to feed people in an emergency.“Historically we have done pretty well coping with specific events such as Covid and we’ve managed to ride through them, but we’re moving into a period where we’re having multiple crises impact at the same time,” says Prof Paul Behrens of the Oxford Martin School, University of Oxford, who signed the letter.These include the worsening climate crisis and increased water scarcity in regions that now provide some of the fresh produce UK households rely on, including the Mediterranean and north Africa.Meanwhile, Behrens and other experts, including Prof Tim Lang of the Centre for Food Policy, City St George’s, University of London, have been warning for some time that the UK’s food distribution network is concentrated, leaving it exposed to potential disruption or targeting by bad actors.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenThe UK’s supermarket network is supplied by just 131 distribution hubs.Photograph: Andy Rain/EPALang has previously stated that the UK’s supermarket network is supplied by just 131 distribution hubs – serving 12,300 stores – while the industry body the Cold Chain Federation has warned that most of Britain’s food imports enter the country through four ports – Dover, Felixstowe, Southampton and London Gateway.The UK governmentwound up the strategic food stockpilethat had been in place since the second world war in the 1990s. Behrens says other nations, particularly Scandinavian countries, now have “far greater national preparedness”.He says: “They’re looking at community responses and how much households can have on hand. They’re looking at their own local production and some countries have strategic stores of grain.”Mother of one Ana, 42, is one of asmall but growing number of citizenswho have been preparing for possible future emergencies for some time. Now living in south Wales, she is originally from eastern Europe and grew up in a family that grew food and preserved it for the colder months. She now shares tips on herYouTube channel, advising other households on resilience and how to build an emergency stockpile.View image in fullscreenAna shares tips on her YouTube channel, advising other households on building resilience and creating an emergency stockpile.Photograph: supplied“It’s just a normal way of life, basically safeguarding yourself and your family,” she says. Ana describes herself as a “prepper”, but wants to move away from its negative connotations, such as panic buying or being a survivalist.“The stereotype was … that preparedness is American, really weird, all camo and blokes in the bushes, hunting and eating squirrels and mushrooms,” she says. Instead she wants to help other citizens learn how they could cope for a few hours, days or even weeks without power, water or being able to get to the shops.“If the stereotype had been dispersed originally by the government, then people would look at preparedness as an everyday thing,” she says.Rob Haward, the chief executive of organic vegetable box delivery company Riverford, believes the UK’s food supply chain needs a “very complicated rethink and a different vision for future security”.Devon-based Riverford distributes about 65,000 boxes a week to customers and about 70% of the produce it sells is grown in the UK, although it also has long-term relationships with growers in Spain and Italy.While the UK is always going to import fruit such as bananas, which cannot be grown in large volumes domestically, Haward believes consumers can also play a role by returning to eating more seasonally.Haward says longer-term contracts can help farmers, giving them confidence to invest in their land and what they grow. He adds: “There are different ways we can try to create a food and farming sector different to now and much more resilient to the future world,” such as working to restore soils to better withstand the changing climate. He also wants government to “pull levers” such as offering lower business rates to greengrocers.Explore more on these topicsUK newsFood & drink industryFarmingRural affairsFoodSupply chain crisisEmergency planningfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: NFL roundup: Daniels’ overtime blunder costs Commanders as Giants salvage wild 27-27 tie | NFL | The Guardian
description: Jayden Daniels runs out the clock with Washington in field-goal range as Giants escape with a 27-27 tie and Patriots cruise past Raiders and Jets stun Cleveland
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Jayden Daniels runs out the clock with Washington in field-goal range as Giants escape with a 27-27 tie and Patriots cruise past Raiders and Jets stun Cleveland
Content: Malik Nabers scores a fourth-quarter touchdown against Commanders cornerback Rasul Douglas as the Giants rallied from 14 points down to earn a 27-27 tie on Sunday in Landover, Maryland.Photograph: Patrick Smith/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMalik Nabers scores a fourth-quarter touchdown against Commanders cornerback Rasul Douglas as the Giants rallied from 14 points down to earn a 27-27 tie on Sunday in Landover, Maryland.Photograph: Patrick Smith/Getty ImagesNFLNFL roundup: Daniels’ overtime blunder costs Commanders as Giants salvage wild 27-27 tieDaniels’ late scramble leaves Washington unable to kickGiants rally from 14 down but settle for 27-27 drawMaye throws four TDs as Patriots rout Raiders 45-17Jaguars stun Eagles in London with one second leftAgenciesSun 11 Oct 2026 17.02 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 19.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJayden Daniels took off on an ill-advised scramble in the closing seconds of overtime with the Commanders in field-goal range, and Washington were unable to stop the clock before time expired, settling for a 27-27 tie with theNew York Giantson Sunday after both teams made critical mistakes in the extra period.Washington (1-3-1) got the ball with two minutes left in overtime when Daron Payne stripped the ball from Cam Skattebo with the Giants in range for a game-winning field goal. Daniels quickly moved the Commanders to the Giants’ 24-yard line, but with 12 seconds left and Washington out of timeouts, he held on to the ball and went down for no gain. Washington lined up to spike the ball, but the clock ticked down to zero and coach Dan Quinn ripped off his headset in disgust.The Commanders had led by two touchdowns in the fourth quarter before Jameis Winston led a furious comeback for the NFC East-leading Giants (3-1-1). He connected with Isaiah Likely for a 17-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter – Likely’s second touchdown catch of the game – and then found Malik Nabers for the tying score, also from 17 yards, with 1:43 remaining.Jaguars stun Eagles in London as Cam Little hits 57-yard winner with one second leftRead moreWinston finished with 326 passing yards and three touchdowns. Daniels threw for 199 yards and rushed for 103 yards and two touchdowns while wearing a brace on his left elbow in his first game back since dislocating it for the second time in Week 2.On a dreary, rainy day at Northwest Stadium, the Giants struggled offensively in the first half but found their rhythm late as Winston led New York to scores on four consecutive possessions.But the Giants also made too many mistakes to come away with the victory. New York’s kicking problems proved costly, with Dominic Zvada converting only two of his five field-goal attempts.Meanwhile, the Giants’ defense struggled to contain Daniels, who rushed for two second-half touchdowns – a 38-yard run in the third quarter that made it 19-6 and a 26-yard score in the fourth that gave the Commanders a seemingly comfortable 27-13 lead.But the Giants rallied behind Winston and his two leading targets, Nabers (11 catches for 121 yards and a touchdown) and Likely (11 receptions for 94 yards and two touchdowns). On his second score, Likely had the ball punched out just after crossing the goal line, but the touchdown was upheld after a replay review.After Nabers’ tying touchdown, the Commanders had one last chance to win in regulation, but their drive stalled at midfield.Las Vegas Raiders 17-45 New England PatriotsDrake Maye threw four touchdown passes and ran for another score as theNew England Patriotsrolled past the Las Vegas Raiders 45-17 on Sunday.Maye completed 26 of 34 passes for 374 yards in the second 300-yard game of his career. Two touchdowns went to Pop Douglas and one each to Hunter Henry and Kyle Williams. Rhamondre Stevenson added a touchdown run.Maye became the first New England quarterback to throw at least three touchdown passes in consecutive games since Tom Brady in 2018. It was also his first turnover-free game of the season. He scored on a three-yard run.The Patriots (3-2) finished with a season-high 536 yards and forced a fumble despite playing without injured receiver Mack Hollins and cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III.Kirk Cousins completed 19 of 28 passes for 243 yards, including a touchdown to Brock Bowers that briefly pulled the Raiders (3-2) level. But Las Vegas did not reach the end zone again until the fourth quarter after scoring at least 26 points in each of their first four games.View image in fullscreenDrake Maye throws a pass under pressure from Raiders defenders during the Patriots’ victory at Gillette Stadium on Sunday in Foxborough, Massachusetts.Photograph: Charles Krupa/APNew York Jets 17-12 Cleveland BrownsBraelon Allen ran 22 yards for the go-ahead touchdown late in the fourth quarter after New York recovered a fumbled punt snap, and the Jets ended a three-game skid with a 17-12 victory over the Cleveland Browns on a rain-soaked Sunday.Rookie David Bailey had three of New York’s eight sacks of Deshaun Watson, and Geno Smith threw a touchdown pass to Garrett Wilson on the Jets’ opening drive, helping snap the Browns’ three-game winning streak.The Browns had a final chance when they got the ball with 1:41 left and no timeouts. But New York’s defense, as they had all game, stiffened and sealed the victory when Will McDonald strip-sacked Watson on fourth down and recovered the fumble.Smith completed 17 of 30 passes for 182 yards and the touchdown to Wilson, who had seven catches for 104 yards. Allen ran for 116 yards and the winning touchdown on 24 carries.It wasn’t pretty, with steady rain falling throughout the game as the remnants of Hurricane Isaias blew through the north-east. But the struggling Jets (2-3) were able to bounce back after surrendering a fourth-quarter lead.Pittsburgh Steelers 34-22 Indianapolis ColtsJaylen Warren piled up 188 total yards and two long touchdowns – one rushing and one receiving – to lead the Pittsburgh Steelers past the Indianapolis Colts 34-22 on Sunday.The Steelers (3-2) shook off a loss at Cleveland by relying on Warren and a defense that frequently bent but rarely broke.Warren caught six passes for 87 yards, including an 80-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the first quarter, and added 101 yards on the ground, highlighted by a 50-yard sprint to the end zone in the third quarter. The typically low-key former undrafted free agent celebrated by hurdling across the goal line.Aaron Rodgers completed 22 of 31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns. While Warren did most of the work on their 80-yard connection, the 42-year-old Rodgers absorbed a crushing hit from 314lb Colts defensive tackle Grover Stewart as he released the ball.Pat Freiermuth caught five passes for 44 yards and two touchdowns for Pittsburgh, the second a 17-yard pass from Rodgers with 6:40 remaining that gave the Steelers enough breathing room to beat the Colts for the 10th time in 12 meetings.Houston Texans 26-3 Tennessee TitansCJ Stroud threw for 261 yards and a touchdown and ran for another score as the Houston Texans snapped their winless start to the season by routing the Tennessee Titans 26-3 on Sunday.It was the second straight season Houston (1-4) ended an opening winless skid by beating Tennessee. This time, the Texans forced two turnovers and Will Anderson Jr had three of Houston’s four sacks. Ka’imi Fairbairn kicked four field goals as the Texans took a 12-3 halftime lead.Houston dominated the second and third quarters, outgaining the Titans 225-49 and outscoring them 16-0. The Texans held Tennessee to a season-low 187 total yards.The Titans (0-5) have now lost 11 straight games in the AFC South and six straight overall dating back to the end of last season.Tennessee led only after opening the game with a drive that ended in a 30-yard field goal by Joey Slye. Cam Ward finished with 170 passing yards.The Texans then forced a three-and-out before safety Jalen Pitre recovered a Tyjae Spears fumble on Tennessee’s next possession. Jake Hansen intercepted Ward on the ensuing drive, and Houston followed by forcing another three-and-out.View image in fullscreenTexans wide receiver Jaylin Noel catches a touchdown pass in front of Titans cornerback Alontae Taylor during the second half of Sunday’s game in Nashville.Photograph: George Walker IV/APMinnesota Vikings 23-13 New Orleans SaintsJustin Jefferson marked his return to Minnesota’s lineup with a leaping touchdown catch, Aaron Jones made up for an early fumble with a pivotal fourth-quarter score and the Vikings remained unbeaten with a 23-13 victory over the slumping New Orleans Saints on Sunday.Will Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts from 40 yards or more for the Vikings (5-0), including a 55-yarder that put Minnesota ahead by 10 in the fourth quarter and all but condemned the Saints (1-4) to a third straight loss, all at the Superdome.Jones finished with 113 rushing yards on 25 carries. Jefferson, who sat out Week 4 with an ankle injury, caught six passes for 79 yards from Kyler Murray, who threw for 229 yards and a touchdown without a turnover and rushed for 51 yards.The Vikings, who entered the game allowing an NFL-low 12.8 points per game, surrendered only one offensive touchdown and held New Orleans to 142 yards.Safety Jonas Sanker returned a fumble 87 yards for the Saints’ other touchdown.Cincinnati Bengals 31-24 Miami DolphinsJoe Burrow threw four touchdown passes, safety Jordan Battle had two interceptions and the Cincinnati Bengals beat the Miami Dolphins 31-24 on Sunday.Ja’Marr Chase, who had been questionable after suffering a concussion last week against Jacksonville, caught six passes for 77 yards, including a spectacular one-handed, 45-yard touchdown catch that made it 28-10.Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards and also threw touchdowns to tight ends Mike Gesicki and Tanner Hudson and running back Samaje Perine. The Bengals quarterback exploited the Dolphins’ young secondary, completing passes to nine different receivers.Battle intercepted Malik Willis on consecutive drives in the second quarter. The safety had said earlier in the week that he had spotted a tell in Willis’s throwing motion, pointing out that the Dolphins quarterback appeared to tap the ball before releasing it.The Dolphins (0-5) pulled within seven points with 45 seconds remaining on Willis’s one-yard touchdown run, set up by a 23-yard catch by rookie Kevin Coleman Jr, who had also caught a touchdown earlier in the fourth quarter. Riley Patterson struck the left upright with the extra-point attempt, and the ensuing onside kick went out of bounds as Cincinnati snapped their two-game skid.Green Bay Packers 31-7 Chicago BearsChristian Watson caught two long touchdown passes from Jordan Love, MarShawn Lloyd also scored twice and the Green Bay Packers exacted a measure of revenge against the Chicago Bears with a 31-7 rout on Sunday.Love completed 25 of 31 passes for 367 yards, the most by a Packers quarterback against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He connected with Watson on a 42-yard touchdown in the first quarter and a 53-yarder in the third.Green Bay had lost three of their previous four meetings with Chicago and squandered a 21-3 halftime lead in a 31-27 NFC wild-card playoff defeat last season. Caleb Williams celebrated that comeback victory by grating cheese on the field, mocking Green Bay’s Cheesehead fanbase.Williams missed a third straight game on Sunday with a hamstring injury, leaving Tyson Bagent to start in his place. Xavier McKinney intercepted two of Bagent’s passes as the Packers forced five turnovers.View image in fullscreenPackers running back MarShawn Lloyd celebrates a rushing touchdown with fans at Lambeau Field during Sunday’s 31-7 victory over the Bears in Green Bay, Wisconsin.Photograph: Daniel Bartel/Getty ImagesDetroit Lions 45-21 Arizona CardinalsJared Goff threw three touchdown passes, Jahmyr Gibbs added 151 yards rushing and two more scores, and the Detroit Lions shook off a slow start by scoring 31 unanswered points to roll past the Arizona Cardinals 45-21 on Sunday.Gibbs barreled into the end zone on a one-yard run in the second quarter and added a three-yard touchdown run in the fourth, bouncing off the offensive line before reversing field and finding room to run. The three-time Pro Bowl selection has scored an NFL-record 58 touchdowns before his 25th birthday, surpassing Lions great Barry Sanders, who had 57.Jameson Williams had his first game with multiple touchdown receptions, catching scoring passes of eight and 39 yards for Detroit (3-2).Arizona (1-4) have lost nine straight home games, a streak stretching back more than a year.It was a disappointing, bizarre afternoon for the Cardinals, who finalized a trade to send receiver Marvin Harrison Jr to the Houston Texans midway through the first quarter. Harrison was one of the team’s five inactive players against the Lions and was not seen at the stadium.Denver Broncos 23-17 Los Angeles ChargersWil Lutz kicked a go-ahead 19-yard field goal with 5:07 remaining, lifting the Denver Broncos to a 23-17 victory over the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.Lutz’s 36-yarder with 1:08 left extended the lead and capped a run of 13 unanswered points in the fourth quarter for the Broncos (3-2).Denver earned their first division win and first victory at SoFi Stadium since 2023, with coach Sean Payton calling the plays. He took those duties away from offensive coordinator Davis Webb earlier in the week. The Broncos won without injured cornerbacks Pat Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs).The Chargers also started 0-5 in 2023, the year before coach Jim Harbaugh took over. They came in with a decimated offensive line featuring four rookies trying to protect quarterback Justin Herbert, who completed 14 of 24 passes for 121 yards, a touchdown and an interception while being sacked five times.Courtland Sutton caught a five-yard touchdown pass from Bo Nix, tying the score at 17 midway through the fourth quarter. The Broncos got the ball back after Herbert came up short on fourth-and-one, and the Chargers sputtered the rest of the way.San Francisco 49ers 32-29 Seattle SeahawksBrock Purdy engineered two scoring drives in the fourth quarter as the San Francisco 49ers rallied to beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 on Sunday, with Eddy Piñeiro kicking a 43-yard field goal with 1:56 remaining.The win for the 49ers (5-0) offered a measure of revenge for their two late-season losses to Seattle (3-2) last season, including a 41-6 defeat in the divisional round of the playoffs with a short-handed roster.San Francisco were healthier for the first meeting this season, and Purdy delivered late as the 49ers opened with five straight wins for the third time in eight seasons.The game featured an NFL season-high seven combined turnovers, the ejection of 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw and no touchdown drives of more than 25 yards before San Francisco took over trailing 26-21 late in the third quarter.Purdy responded with an impressive drive against Seattle’s vaunted defense, including a 28-yard pass to Mike Evans after an intentional grounding penalty left the 49ers facing second-and-21.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsNew England PatriotsLas Vegas RaidersNew York GiantsDallas CowboysShareReuse this content

title: Cherki cracker caps Manchester City win at Liverpool in face of Anfield taunts | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Erling Haaland and Jérémy Doku were also on target in Manchester City’s 3-0 win against Liverpool, who had Ryan Gravenberch sent off after 62 minutes
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Erling Haaland and Jérémy Doku were also on target in Manchester City’s 3-0 win against Liverpool, who had Ryan Gravenberch sent off after 62 minutes
Content: Rayan Cherki is congratulated by Jérémy Doku and Enzo Fernández after scoring Manchester City’s third goal.Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenRayan Cherki is congratulated by Jérémy Doku and Enzo Fernández after scoring Manchester City’s third goal.Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueCherki cracker caps Manchester City win at Liverpool in face of Anfield tauntsDavid Hytnerat AnfieldSun 11 Oct 2026 13.42 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt is a soundtrack thatManchester Cityhave heard before but never for such sustained spells during a match. It came from the Liverpool support, first ringing out around Anfield before kick-off and coming at regular intervals thereafter.It was always going to be like this as City felt their way intoa new reality, one conditioned by the guilty verdicts handed to them by an independent commission on virtually all of the 115 charges they have faced for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules. City maintain their innocence and have appealed.Tension, ‘cheat’ banners and inflatable bananas: Manchester City’s welcome to AnfieldRead moreThe Kop wanted to tell City what they are. And where they were going. They wanted to tell them again and again. According to them, they are cheats, who are set to be relegated. It was not exactly a bear pit of an atmosphere; not truly intimidating. It was just an outpouring of anger and it was impossible to ignore.City did not care. They rolled with the invective. And after a slow-burn contest turned on a second yellow card for the Liverpool midfielder, Ryan Gravenberch, in the 62nd minute, City cut loose. All that their players can do is try to blot out the noise. They did so here, running all over Liverpool’s 10 men to maintain their 100% start to thePremier Leagueseason. The key theme from them – and their fans – was defiance. City intend to keep doing what they do.It was Erling Haaland, inevitably, who lashed them in front and Jérémy Doku, on as a game-changing substitute in the 56th minute, who curled them further ahead with a beauty. The best was still to come. Again, Doku was involved. And after Rayan Cherki dummied a pass from Elliot Anderson, he ran on to a backheel from another substitute, Josko Gvardiol. Cherki had work to do. He did it when he cut away from Jeremie Frimpong, on as a substitute, and rolled home. It was a team goal marked by individual brilliance.Liverpool were broken and en route to a first defeat under Andoni Iraola. The manager was undermined by the absence of arguably his three best players so far this season; Dominik Szoboszlai, Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak all picked up injuries during the international window.Liverpoollacked punch.City had reason to curse the timing of this fixture. Apart from Manchester United at Old Trafford, it could hardly have been worse than a visit here. And not only because Liverpool were one of the clubs most seriously undermined by their accountancy practices. City sneaked their team buses around the back of the stadium on the way in, avoiding the jibes from the streets, but it only postponed the inevitable. It was always going to be lively.When the Premier League published the document thatprovided the first raft of detailabout the decisions against City on the Tuesday before last, it hit hard. It was the weight of the language – how it dripped with contempt – as well as the sheer extent of the transgressions. Proven misconduct. Sham arrangements. Concerted attempts to frustrate the investigation. How some of the club’s witnesses gave evidence that they knew to be untrue. It served to frame this game. It will continue to frame each one that City play for the foreseeable.View image in fullscreenJérémy Doku doubles Manchester City’s lead with a stunning curling shot.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesThe City fans came armed with scores of inflatable bananas. Some of them wore old-school replica shirts. There was a message in there somewhere. Maybe to say that their club predates the Abu Dhabi takeover. It was also possible to spot banners in support of Khaldoon al-Mubarak, the club chair.You want banners? The Kop had that boxed off. There were some that riffed off Oasis lyrics, including one with the line that “after all, you really robbed us all”. The most eye-catching was unfurled before kick-off, featuring the word ‘cheats’ and a very long sequence of pound signs.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThere was very little to report in terms of first-half action. Even the melee that broke out in the 12th minute after Alexis Mac Allister tussled with Anderson was the definition of handbags. There were no big chances; the precision on the final ball was frequently absent.Iraola gave Lewis Koumas a full league debut up front and it was the 21-year-old who had the first decent effort straight after the restart. Gianluigi Donnarumma stood tall to save. Liverpool upped the intensity and they had a spell where they pushed and the Kop felt the breakthrough was coming. Gravenberch worked Donnarumma. Mac Allister volleyed wide.View image in fullscreenRyan Gravenberch (right) walks off after receiving a red card from the referee Chris Kavanagh.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesHaaland blew a glorious chance from an Antoine Semenyo pass on the hour, dinking past the far post but City had otherwise created little. Then everything changed. Gravenberch caught the eye with his surging runs but he was on the wrong side when he challenged Doku, who was ready to spark a counterattack. It was clumsy from the Dutchman, the contact on Doku not exactly strong. But having been booked at the start of the second half for a foul on Anderson, Gravenberch was running an almighty risk. He did not get away with it.City had their opening and how they piled through it. The way that they overwhelmed Liverpool was really something; a demonstration of their strength. It was not a game for the neutral. Are there any such viewers where City are concerned any more? Doku almost teed up Nico O’Reilly and City were on their way when Haaland swept home from a deflected Doku cross. A new reality? It was the same old City on the pitch.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueLiverpoolManchester Citymatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Canelo Álvarez ‘fears nothing’ and will fight in Riyadh despite deadly attacks, Al-Sheikh says | Canelo Álvarez | The Guardian
description: Turki al-Sheikh says Mexican star remains committed to 31 October bout with Christian Mbilli despite escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Author: Bryan Armen Graham
Headline: Turki al-Sheikh says Mexican star remains committed to 31 October bout with Christian Mbilli despite escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Content: Turki al-Sheikh (left) watches Canelo Álvarez ahead of his super-middleweight fight against William Scull in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in May 2025.Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTurki al-Sheikh (left) watches Canelo Álvarez ahead of his super-middleweight fight against William Scull in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in May 2025.Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty ImagesCanelo ÁlvarezCanelo Álvarez ‘fears nothing’ and will fight in Riyadh despite deadly attacks, Al-Sheikh saysÁlvarez vows to fight in Riyadh despite deadly strikesAirport attacks leave at least 12 dead, hundreds hurtMexican seeks redemption after Crawford defeatBryan Armen Grahamand agenciesSun 11 Oct 2026 16.42 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 16.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCanelo Álvarez intends to go ahead with his world title fight in Saudi Arabia later this month despite a series of deadly attacks on airports and other infrastructure in the kingdom, according toTurki al-Sheikh, the Saudi official who has become one of boxing’s most influential power brokers.The Mexican superstar is slated to challenge the unbeaten Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh on 31 October, three weeks after Saturday’s missile strike on the Saudi capital’s main international airportkilled at least 12 peopleand wounded more than 300.Houthi attack on Riyadh airport forces swift rethink of Trump’s new strategyRead moreAl-Sheikh, the chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, said on Sunday that Álvarez had personally assured him he remained committed to the bout regardless of the fraught security situation.“Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” Al-Sheikhwrote on social media. “He fears nothing. My country is home to the two Holy Mosques, land of peace, safety, rich civilization, deep history and kind-hearted people. Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends.”The reassurance came as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels intensified their attacks on Saudi territory. Asecond projectile struck a passenger terminalat King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, according to the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen. Authorities reported further injuries but did not immediately provide a figure.View image in fullscreenA person watches Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea deliver a televised statement in Sana’a on Sunday, claiming responsibility for missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including a deadly strike on Riyadh’s international airport.Photograph: Yahya Arhab/EPASaturday’s strike, which hit the same airport complex, was the deadliest attack on a Gulf Arab country since the outbreak of the war with Iran. India’s embassy subsequently reported that one of its citizens had died from injuries sustained in the attack, potentially raising the death toll to 13.The airport remained closed on Sunday, while the US government has urged American citizens to avoid the facility and its surrounding area. Several international airlines have suspended flights to Saudi Arabia amid the mounting threat to civilian aviation.Is Fury v Joshua about meritocratic sporting excellence or just algorithmic celebrity power? | Jonathan LiewRead moreThe Houthis, who have claimed responsibility for attacks on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom, have warned airlines and travelers against entering Saudi airspace. The escalation has raised concerns about the safety of major international events in a country thathas invested heavily in establishing itselfas a destination for global sport, entertainment and business.Saudi Arabiahas become a major force in professional boxingunder Al-Sheikh, staging a succession of high-profile bouts in Riyadh and using its considerable financial resources to attract some of the sport’s biggest names. The kingdom’s expanding sporting ambitions have also drawn scrutiny over its human rights record andaccusations of sportswashing.The latest attacks threaten those ambitions at a particularly sensitive moment. Saudi Arabia is hosting an international energy conference this week, with further major business gatherings scheduled, while the widening conflict has raised the possibility of greater US military involvement. US president Donald Trump said on Saturday that he was considering action against the Houthis and planned to speak with Saudi Crown PrinceMohammed bin Salman.Álvarez, 36, has a professional record of 63 wins, three defeats and two draws, including 39 knockouts. The 31 October contest would mark his return to the ring for the first time sincelosing a unanimous decision to Terence Crawfordin September 2025. He previously fought in Riyadh in May of that year.View image in fullscreenCanelo Álvarez is scheduled to return to the ring against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on 31 October, his first fight since losing a unanimous decision to Terence Crawford in September 2025.Photograph: Steve Marcus/Getty ImagesSpeaking on a Zoom call with the Guardian and other reporters on Tuesday, Álvarez admitted that his focus had wavered in the days leading up to the Crawford fight, despite what he described as a strong training camp.“When you lose, you always look back and look [at] your mistakes,” Álvarez said. “I did a very good preparation for [the] Crawford fight, but in the fight week, my mind wasn’t there.”The former undisputed super-middleweight champion has been preparing for his comeback on Spain’s Mediterranean coast, training at the same facility used by Oleksandr Usyk. He has also adjusted his schedule to account for the time difference in Saudi Arabia, having struggled to acclimatize during his previous visit. Álvarez said he now believes he needs 21 days to adjust fully to the change in time zones.Mbilli, who has won all 29 of his professional fights, 24 by knockout, represents another formidable challenge. Álvarez described him as a relentless, high-volume puncher whose aggressive style should make for a crowd-pleasing contest.Álvarez, who turned professional at 15, also declined to put a timetable on his retirement when asked how much longer he intended to compete.“I don’t know how many more fights,” he said. “I don’t know because I feel really good.”Explore more on these topicsCanelo ÁlvarezTurki al-SheikhBoxingMiddle East and north AfricaHouthisSaudi ArabiaYemenShareReuse this content

title: Kyrie Irving returns from 20-month injury layoff with vintage display in Macau | Kyrie Irving | The Guardian
description: Kyrie Irving scored 17 points in his first game since tearing his ACL in March 2025, helping Dallas beat Houston 132-115 in a pre-season exhibition in China
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Kyrie Irving scored 17 points in his first game since tearing his ACL in March 2025, helping Dallas beat Houston 132-115 in a pre-season exhibition in China
Content: Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving drives to the basket against the Rockets during Sunday’s NBA pre-season game at the Venetian Arena in Macao, China. Irving scored 17 points in his first game since tearing his ACL in March 2025.Photograph: Juan Ocampo/NBAE/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMavericks guard Kyrie Irving drives to the basket against the Rockets during Sunday’s NBA pre-season game at the Venetian Arena in Macao, China. Irving scored 17 points in his first game since tearing his ACL in March 2025.Photograph: Juan Ocampo/NBAE/Getty ImagesKyrie IrvingKyrie Irving returns from 20-month injury layoff with vintage display in MacauMavericks star dazzles in return from ACL tearIrving scores 17 points in Dallas’s 132-115 winDusty May hails nine-time All-Star as an ‘artist’AgenciesSun 11 Oct 2026 15.18 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKyrie Irving waited nearly 600 days for his return to the NBA. TheDallas Mavericksdidn’t keep him waiting any longer for his welcome-back basket.Irving scored a reverse layup on the game’s opening possession on Sunday night, setting the tone for a team-high 17 points in the Mavericks’ 132-115 pre-season win over theHouston Rocketsin Macau.It was Irving’s first game action since he tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee on 3 March 2025.‘I’m supposed to be here’: Angel Reese’s road from ridicule to the WNBA finalsRead more“It was just impressive,” Dallas coach Dusty May told reporters at a postgame press conference. “His physical condition, his mental condition, and then – I’ve said it from the first time I watched him in a workout – he’s an artist. He’s a jazz musician. ... I didn’t expect him to play this well after being off so long.”Irving shot six for 13 in just under 22 minutes, adding three assists and two rebounds. Dallas won the opening tip, and reigning rookie of the year Cooper Flagg set up Irving on the right wing. Irving didn’t hesitate, driving towards the baseline before scoring with a reverse layup.The Mavericks’ bench immediately erupted in celebration, while the roar of the crowd in China – where the Rockets are among the most popular teams, largely because of Chinese superstar, former Houston great andBasketballHall of Famer Yao Ming – was noticeable as well.“Grateful that Dusty called the first play for me,” Irving said. “Had my mind made up, just to attack. ... I was imagining how it was going to go, dreaming about how it was going to go and just glad that I got that out the way. Just incredibly grateful for my teammates as well and their support and just seeing them rise up off the bench to celebrate me as well, that always feels good. And God is truly the greatest. So just being able to perform at a high level, that felt amazing.”Irving missed all of last season, meaning it had been just over 20 months since he last played in a game.The nine-time All-Star was averaging 24.7 points for Dallas when he was injured late in the 2024-25 season, and anything close to that production this season would provide a welcome boost to a franchise that reached theNBAfinals in 2024 but missed the last two postseasons.View image in fullscreenMavericks guard Kyrie Irving helps teammate Cooper Flagg to his feet during Sunday’s NBA pre-season game against the Rockets at the Venetian Arena in Macau.Photograph: Zhizhao Wu/Getty Images“It’s always great to see somebody coming from the injury that Ky came from to get back on the court,” Houston guard Marcus Smart said. “I know we compete, but you want to compete against the best and you want everybody to be out there. For him to be back out there, it was great to see. He looked good, but we expected him to look good. Very happy for him.”Irving played eight minutes in the first quarter, a little more than eight in the second and returned for the first five and a half minutes of the third before sitting out the remainder of the game.Irving is enormously popular in China, which he has visited many times over the years and plans to return to in 2027 as part of his annual world tour. He thanked fans who gathered outside the Mavericks’ hotel to show their support or sent good-luck messages on social media.“It’s definitely a lot of emotions that were going into it,” Irving said. “Looking forward to getting back home and continuing to carry on what we learned here from each other.”Explore more on these topicsKyrie IrvingNBABasketballUS sportsDallas MavericksHouston RocketsShareReuse this content

title: Resurgent Verstappen holds off Leclerc to seal dominant F1 Singapore GP win | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: Max Verstappen dominated the Singapore Grand Prix to claim his second victory in a row for Red Bull ahead of Charles Leclerc and the championship leader Kimi Antonelli
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Max Verstappen dominated the Singapore Grand Prix to claim his second victory in a row for Red Bull ahead of Charles Leclerc and the championship leader Kimi Antonelli
Content: Max Verstappen crosses the line to complete a perfect weekend at the Singapore Grand Prix.Photograph: Peter Fox/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMax Verstappen crosses the line to complete a perfect weekend at the Singapore Grand Prix.Photograph: Peter Fox/Getty ImagesFormula One 2026Resurgent Verstappen holds off Leclerc to seal dominant F1 Singapore GP winRed Bull driver claims second victory in a rowKimi Antonelli third and closes in on titleGiles RichardsSun 11 Oct 2026 10.19 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 14.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDelivering an emphatic reminder of how imperious he can be when he has the car beneath him, Max Verstappenwas untouchable in victoryat the Singapore Grand Prix.It has takenRed Bullmost of the season to deliver said ride, however, and the title is beyond the Dutchman. In his wake at the Marina Bay circuit the champion in waiting, Kimi Antonelli, did enough to move to within a race of taking the crown.Kimi Antonelli admits he can taste F1 glory after Verstappen wins Singapore GPRead moreThe race under the floodlights certainly belonged to Verstappen, who with a commanding run from pole to flag took his first victory at Marina Bay, on the occasion of his 250th race.He was enthused, understandably. Having wrestled with a recalcitrant car for so long, the Red Bull was purring in Singapore. He took pole and thewin in the sprint raceand then pole and victory in the grand prix.His second win in a row this season was taken with consummate calm even given a malfunctioning radio, where all the team could hear from him was the garbled, distorted static beloved of the more vociferous noise metal outfits.The victory, beating theFerrariof Charles Leclerc into second place with Antonelli taking third, was of greatest import in that he and the team have proved able to bring performance to the car that they can feed into next year’s model.On this form they can expect to open 2027 in a far more competitive position, from which Verstappen will expect not to be on the sidelines of a title fight, a fight that this time around has been absolutely bossed by Antonelli.His third place in Singapore, along with his Mercedes teammate George Russell coming back to take only ninth place, having started from 19th, was enough to ensure the 20-year-old has one hand on the title.His lead over Russell is now 102 points and he can mathematically win the title at the next round in Austin if he takes victory and Russell finishes ninth or lower andLewis Hamilton, who was sixth in Singapore and is 111 in arrears, is fifth or lower.The Italian reacted with surprise when told he could seal it and become F1’s youngest champion as soon as Texas. He was counting no chickens but there was, for the first time, an acknowledgment that his dream is within reach.View image in fullscreenMax Verstappen leading the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton.Photograph: Jakub Porzycki/ReutersThe manner of how he reached this point was demonstrated in Singapore, where he ground out the best he could with a car that was not competitive at the very front while notably enjoying, as all champions do, a little good fortune as well.In what was a largely pedestrian race on a track where passing is remarkably tricky and with Verstappen in a class of his own out front, Antonelli understood that banking points from fourth on the grid was all that mattered and proceeded to pound round in a strategic fight with the Ferraris of Leclerc and Hamilton and the McLaren of Lando Norris.He complained of feeling liquid at his feet and losing his brakes at one point but held his nerve with the steel of a veteran. Solid but unspectacular, he was in fifth for much of the race until the final stages when Hamilton’s decision not to pit under a virtual safety car came back and bit the Ferrari driver.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHis tyres gone, Hamilton’s pace fell away and he was caught by Norris and Antonelli in the final laps. Norris attacked the Ferrari but in the process was mugged by the Italian, for whom a sniff of a chance yawns open with barn door proportions. Through he nipped and third was his.Quick GuideF1 Singapore GP results and standingsShow1Max Verstappen🇳🇱Red Bull1:42:00.785 –25pts2Charles Leclerc🇲🇨Ferrari+7.335 –18pts3Kimi Antonelli🇮🇹Mercedes+34.573 –15pts4Lando Norris🇬🇧McLaren+40.506 –12pts5Oscar Piastri🇦🇺McLaren+49.644 –10pts6Lewis Hamilton🇬🇧Ferrari+53.188 –8pts7Liam Lawson🇳🇿Red Bull+81.386 –6pts8Nico Hülkenberg🇩🇪Audi+66.187 –4pts9George Russell🇬🇧Mercedes+84.677 –2pts10Isack Hadjar🇫🇷Red Bull+90.862–1pt11Pierre Gasly🇫🇷Alpine+1 lap12Oliver Bearman🇬🇧Haas+1 lap13Esteban Ocon🇫🇷Haas+1 lap14Carlos Sainz🇪🇸Williams+1 lap15Arvid Lindblad🇬🇧Racing Bulls+1 lap16Fernando Alonso🇪🇸Aston Martin+1 lap17Sergio Pérez🇲🇽Cadillac+2 laps18Alexander Albon🇹🇭WilliamsDNF19Valtteri Bottas🇫🇮Cadillac+3 lapsNCLance Stroll🇨🇦Aston MartinDNFNCFranco Colapinto🇦🇷AlpineDNFNCGabriel Bortoleto🇧🇷AudiDNFDrivers' championship1 Kimi Antonelli 340pts, 2 George Russell 238, 3 Lewis Hamilton 229, 4 Max Verstappen 221, 5 Charles Leclerc 215, 6 Lando Norris 201, 7 Oscar Piastri  138, 8 Isack Hadjar 97, 9 Liam Lawson 75, 10 Pierre Gasly 41, 11 Arvid Lindblad 38, 12 Franco Colapinto 27, 13 Oliver Bearman 23, 14 Nico Hulkenberg 13, 15 Gabriel Bortoleto 10, 16 Esteban Ocon 7, 17 Fernando Alonso 7, 18 Carlos Sainz 7, 19 Alexander Albon 5, 20 Yuki Tsunoda 1Constructors' championship1 Mercedes 578pts, 2 Ferrari 444, 3 McLaren 339, 4 Red Bull 332, 5 Racing Bulls 100, 6 Alpine 68, 7 Haas 30, 8 Audi 23, 9 Williams 12, 10 Aston Martin 7Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.It enlivened what was an otherwise lacklustre affair and, with Russell stymied in ninth behind the Audi of Nico Hülkenberg, the numbers were suddenly adding up for Antonelli. Austin beckons and, if not there, Mexico a week later will likely see his coronation complete.View image in fullscreenMax Verstappen celebrates his victory, his first in Singapore.Photograph: David Davies/PANorris went on to take fourth, with his teammate Oscar Piastri in fifth, both having dispensed with Hamilton who by then was crawling round, the rubber he had made last for 42 laps now shot.Hamilton had started third but took his pit stop early in the race after which Ferrari appeared to be undecided as to fully commit him to a two-stop strategy, notably not calling for Leclerc to move over for him.All of which was compounded when Hamilton decided for them, opting not to pit under a virtual safety car, despite his team being ready for him. For which he held his hands up . “Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy,” he said. “My call, and I lost us valuable points. I’ll try and make up for it in the next one.”Another debrief required for Ferrari then as F1 adjusts to what appears to be the new pecking order, with Verstappen and Red Bull at the sharp end, but Antonelli now very much ready to make history.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportMax VerstappenLewis HamiltonRed BullFerrarinewsShareReuse this content

title: Taylor Knibb wins Ironman world title after leader collapses in dramatic Kona finish | Triathlon | The Guardian
description: American triathlete claims first Hawaiian Ironman crown after defending champion Solveig Løvseth collapses within sight of finish
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: American triathlete claims first Hawaiian Ironman crown after defending champion Solveig Løvseth collapses within sight of finish
Content: Taylor Knibb celebrates after winning the women’s Ironman World Championship in Kailua-Kona, Hawaii, on Saturday.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images for IRONMANView image in fullscreenTaylor Knibb celebrates after winning the women’s Ironman World Championship in Kailua-Kona, Hawaii, on Saturday.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images for IRONMANTriathlonTaylor Knibb wins Ironman world title after leader collapses in dramatic Kona finishKnibb overtakes Norwegian rival in final kilometerDefending champion Løvseth collapses while leadingFrance’s Vincent Luis wins men’s title on Kona debutRoger VaughanSun 11 Oct 2026 10.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAmerican triathlete Taylor Knibb has won her first Hawaiian Ironman world title after one of the most dramatic finishes in race history.With a mile left, Norwegian defending champion Solveig Løvseth led Knibb by more than a minute and looked rock-solid, having taken the lead from her inside the final 10km of the 42.2km marathon run.But then Løvseth quickly developed a dramatic case of the wobbles and collapsed. Knibb passed her about a kilometre from the finish and the Norwegian eventually recovered from the meltdown to finish eighth.It recalled the 1995 race, when Paula Newby-Fraser collapsed within just 500m of her seventh win and was passed by Karen Smyers.In a twist of history, Smyers helped hold the winner’s tape for Knibb.Vincent Luis of France won the men’s race aged 37, on his debut. It was just his third Ironman-distance race after Luis won Olympic bronze at Tokyo in the mixed team relay and claimed the 2019 and 2020 world championship series titles.View image in fullscreenTaylor Knibb competes during the marathon leg of the Ironman World Championship in Kailua-Kona, Hawaii, on Saturday.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty Images for IRONMANGrace Thek was the best-placed Australian, rallying in the marathon to finish 10th on her debut at Kona. Nick Thompson finished 11th among the professional men.Essendon’s David Zaharakis joined a select group of former AFL players to finish Hawaii as an age-group competitor.Knibb had to pull out of the race a year ago with only a couple of kilometres left, while in the lead.But on Sunday (AEST), the American showed she had learned her painful lessons, staying composed when Løvseth passed her.Knibb won the 3.8km swim, 180km cycle and 42.2km run event – triathlon’s most famous race – in eight hours, 36 minutes and 29 seconds. Germany’s Laura Philipp was three minutes back in second.Løvseth was able to walk to the finish, smiling and high-fiving fans. Always a tough race, Hawaii this year was marked by particularly high humidity, and several contenders either did not finish or hit the wall.Allow Instagram content?This article includes content provided byInstagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continue“Last year played a huge part because ... I made a big decision and it was just, ‘take care of yourself’, because it was getting really hard,” Knibb said.“Then when Solveig came back, I thought I can’t fight because if I fight, I’m going to lose, so I had to learn from last year to just get to the finish line, get to the finish line, get to the finish line.”Luis had said before his Kona debut that he would also retire afterwards. He will now reconsider.The Frenchman held off hard-charging Norwegian Gustav Iden, the 2022 winner, to claim the world title in 7hr 47min 27sec. Iden finished runner-up in 7:49:03.“I said if I win, I will maybe not continue, but I went through some dark places in the last 3-4km – but 100% worth it,” Luis said.“Let’s see, I have a few nights out to decide what to do with my life now.”Explore more on these topicsTriathlonAthleticsUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Williams strikes out 12 as Guardians blank White Sox to complete ALDS comeback | MLB | The Guardian
description: Cleveland rally from 2-0 down to win decisive Game 5 against Chicago and advance to ALCS against Tampa Bay behind dominant pitching from Gavin Williams
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Cleveland rally from 2-0 down to win decisive Game 5 against Chicago and advance to ALCS against Tampa Bay behind dominant pitching from Gavin Williams
Content: The Guardians’ José Ramírez celebrates after hitting a two-run home run during the fourth inning of Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday night in Cleveland.Photograph: Jason Miller/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe Guardians’ José Ramírez celebrates after hitting a two-run home run during the fourth inning of Game 5 of the American League Division Series on Saturday night in Cleveland.Photograph: Jason Miller/Getty ImagesMLBWilliams strikes out 12 as Guardians blank White Sox to complete ALDS comebackWilliams fans 12 as Cleveland win decisive Game 5Ramírez’s two-run homer provides only scoringGuardians to face Rays for place in World SeriesAgenciesSat 10 Oct 2026 22.58 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 11.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGavin Williams struck out 12, José Ramírez homered on a pitch just above home plate and theCleveland Guardiansbeat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 on Saturday night to complete a comeback from a 2-0 deficit in their best-of-five American League Division Series.Cleveland open the American League Championship Series at Tampa Bay on Monday night, seeking their first World Series appearance since 2016. The Guardians/Indians franchise have not won the title since 1948, the longest drought amongMLBteams.Guardians pitchers struck out 21, the most in a nine-inning postseason game. The White Sox managed just three hits, putting only nine balls in play, and struck out 75 times over the series.Two days after getting the save in Game 4, Williams became just the third pitcher in postseason history to get the last out of a game and start the following game when his team faced elimination in both.He did not allow a hit until Kyle Teel looped a knuckle-curve into right field with two outs in the sixth, two innings after Ramírez homered for the second straight game, a two-run drive off Sean Burke.After a walk loaded the bases, Erik Sabrowski relieved Williams and struck out Munetaka Murakami.Williams’s 12 strikeouts tied Cleveland’s record for a postseason game. He got 22 swings and misses, and his 24 strikeouts over three games tied for the second most in a best-of-five postseason series.Hunter Gaddis followed Sabrowski and got four outs. Cade Smith finished for his first career five-out save, striking out the side in the ninth. He blew a fastball by Tristan Peters for the final out, setting off a celebration at Progressive Field.Chicago, the first team to reach the playoffs after three straight 100-loss seasons, have not won the World Series since 2005.Explore more on these topicsMLBCleveland GuardiansChicago White SoxBaseballUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘That’s when I begin to scream’: Mick Fanning on punching a great white shark | Mick Fanning | The Guardian
description: The Australian surfing champion was monstered by a great white shark in 2015 in the middle of a competition in South Africa. Here, he relives the encounter
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Australian surfing champion was monstered by a great white shark in 2015 in the middle of a competition in South Africa. Here, he relives the encounter
Content: Australian surfer Mick Fanning moments before he fought off a shark during the J-Bay Open competition in Jeffreys Bay, South Africa, on 19 July 2015. The attack is recounted in his new memoir, All Heart.Photograph: WSL/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAustralian surfer Mick Fanning moments before he fought off a shark during the J-Bay Open competition in Jeffreys Bay, South Africa, on 19 July 2015. The attack is recounted in his new memoir, All Heart.Photograph: WSL/AFP/Getty ImagesMick Fanning‘That’s when I begin to scream’: Mick Fanning on punching a great white sharkThe Australian surfing champion was monstered by a great white shark while competing against fellow Aussie Julian Wilson in the 2015 world tour event final at Jeffreys Bay in South Africa. The attack was broadcast live on TV. Here, in an extract from his memoir, All Heart, he relives the encounterMick FanningSun 11 Oct 2026 10.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 19.23 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleI’m locked in on my take-off spot in the J-Bay lineup, scanning the horizon, biding my time. Assessing my position against the rippling lines of the oncoming set, I decide to move slightly further inside.As I move, there’s a big splash behind me. Glancing over my left shoulder, I catch a glimpse of a huge dark shape in the water. A jolt of fear grips me. What the hell is that?Instinct kicks in and I haul myself up on to my board to shield my body. There’s a violent lurch directly beneath me. Suddenly, I’m yanked off by a wild tug on my leg rope. I quickly scramble to get back on my board and that’s when I see it. The unmistakable fin of a shark.There’s a split second of full-body panic. Then: THWACK! The shark’s tail whips out and wallops my left cheek. My head jerks back as a white flash of pain explodes in my skull. Then I’m being dragged down into the churning water, the force almost tearing my leg from its socket. Consumed with terror, I’m suddenly released and break through to the surface, gasping for breath. Has the shark got tangled in my leg rope and bitten through it?Suddenly, the shark jackknifes around. It’s like a torpedo hurtling straight towards me. That’s when I begin to scream.View image in fullscreen‘There’s a split second of full-body panic. Then: THWACK!’Photograph: AFP/Getty ImagesThe shark crashes into me from the side and I blindly lash out with my fists, yelling, punching, kicking. It shrugs me off like a leaf. I fall backwards into the waves again and as my head surfaces, I see it swimming away from me towards the horizon.Flailing in the water, head on a swivel, I swim away hard. I can see Jules about 25 metres away now.In my years of spearfishing, I’ve never encountered more sharks than now. But I know where I stand in the underwater pecking order | Clarke GayfordRead moreGot to warn him. Now. “Shark! Shark! Go in! Go!
