GO!”Jules keeps paddling towards me. “Go in!” I yell.“There’s a bloody shark.” He keeps coming.Just then, I imagine the shark circling back around. If it comes for me now, it’ll get me from behind. I’ve got no board, it’ll go at my legs first. There’s no way to defend myself. Fuck that.There’s no way I’m going to let that happen. I stop swimming. Force myself to turn. Fists clenched, I tread water breathing hard, trying to get as high as I can, scouring the water for the shark’s return. The world goes mute and I’m so focused that I don’t notice the jetski until it’s right by my side.“Mick! Mick! Get up here!”Surfer Mick Fanning fights off shark attack at J-Bay OpenGuardianI scramble up on to the sled it’s towing, looking around for Jules. “Jules? Where is he?”“On the other jetski. He’s fine. You OK?”Wait, am I OK? Hastily, I scan my limbs. Check my hands and fingers, feet and toes. I seem to be alright. I just need to stop hyperventilating.“Yeah, I’m OK. But what the fuck?”Seconds later, the jetski pulls up by the bigger boat. Jules is on board. His eyes are wild. “You right?” he stammers.“Yeah, you? I was telling you to go in! You crazy bastard.”He shrugs and then gripping each other by the shoulders, we both start laughing manically, shit-faced on adrenaline and pure relief. “That was so gnarly. So fucking gnarly.”“Whoah! I can’t believe that actually happened.” And it’s like we’ve survived the biggest scare of all time. Like we’ve won a war, cheated death, escaped the jaws of a great white! Somehow, we’ve got away scot-free. There are high fives and backslaps. Hoots and howls. Everyone on the boat is talking a mile a minute, pumped up with a mix of exhilaration and hysteria.“If you’re both OK, we’re going to get you in now,” says Peter Mel, the field commentator who’s been calling heats from the water.“We can probably just surf in, yeah?”Peter stares at me as if I’m insane, then he speaks to me with the sort of soft tone you’d use to address a small child.“No, Mick, that was a big shark. We’re going to escort you in.”Whatever. I turn to Jules. “I can’t believe you fucking swum towards me. You’re fucking crazy!”“What was I gonna do? Watch my mate get eaten by a shark?”On the shore, we’re bustled straight into a white Volkswagen van and continue our postmortem. When Jules hears that I punched the shark, he convulses in giggles. I laugh too, because it’s all so crazy. Jules still looks utterly wired, his pupils dilated like two black holes.“Mate, that was wild!” he says shaking his head.View image in fullscreenMick Fanning, left, embraces fellow surfer Julian Wilson after the shark attack.Photograph: Kirstin Scholtz/AFP/Getty ImagesI start laughing again. It’s like my nervous system has got whiplash. Then the doors of the van open.Standing outside are Jarrad and Fletch, plus my mates: Otto, Ace and a bunch of other touring surfers. I’m expecting more high fives and wild-eyed grins. Instead, they’re deathly quiet. They look shell-shocked and upset. In fact, most of them are in tears.double quotation markSuddenly, I don’t feel invincible any more. I just feel very, very luckyMick FanningOK, maybe I’ve misread the situation here …I’m engulfed in a tearful hug from Ace[Australian world tour surfer Adrian Buchan]. He’s more distraught than I am. Then Fletch embraces me [Rip Curl team manager Ryan Fletcher]. Then Jarrad[former tour surfer and Mick’s coach at the event]. Immediately, I start explaining what happened. How the shark grabbed my leg rope. Bit through it. How I landed a punch or two.“Someone was looking after us,” I say.Jules and I are led up to the commissioner’s office. Inside, they’re all completely rattled too. I get hugged by more people. I agree to an interview with Ronnie who is there in his role as an event commentator for the WSL broadcast. It hadn’t occurred to me yet that this whole thing has been beamed live all around the world. As Fletch suggests: it’s the easiest way to let everyone back home know I’m OK.Before the interview I’m asked by the tour commissioner, Kieren Perrow, if I’d like to see the footage.“Yeah, I think I’ve got to,” I tell him. “Cause I don’t think I’m processing this the same as everyone else.”Shark attack on surfer Mick Fanning: I punched it a couple of timesGuardianIn Kieren’s office, a bunch of us gather around a big-screen TV. And then, I watch the replay.There I am waiting for a wave, oblivious. Then the splash behind me, the shark’s fin, the flurry of whitewater as I try to scramble away. The next moment, a wave obscures the camera. For eight long seconds no one can see the frantic tussle that almost cost me my life. The camera even pans back as if wanting to protect the viewer from the worst-case scenario.“We all thought you were gone,” Jarrad says. “The last thing we saw was you being knocked off your board, then that set rolled in. Next thing we saw was your board heading out to sea … ”View image in fullscreenPhotograph: Simon & SchusterWatching the footage, what’s most terrifying is the size of the shark. It must’ve been at least three-and-a-half metres long, with the girth of a submarine. Suddenly, I don’t feel invincible any more. I just feel very, very lucky. A shark that big can do whatever the hell it wants.“Oh fuck,” I stammer.And suddenly it dawns on me that Mum was watching the final live back home.“Can someone please call Mum? Let her know I’m OK.”Then I realise the quickest way to let her know is to jump on the broadcast, which is still going. I do the interview with Ronnie. The adrenaline is starting to wear off now, the cold horror of what happened is kicking in. The conversation is a blur. I’m just about holding it together, wiping away the odd tear.“The commissioner’s office has decided that there’ll be no final run today,” Ronnie says.“Is that even a concern for you at this stage?”“Mate, I’m happy to not ever compete again. I just want to let all my family and friends know that I’m OK. Right now, I’m just tripping out.”The interview finishes, and as I walk off camera, standing there is Kelly Slater. He’s my arch rival, the man I’ve battled against so hard on so many occasions. He walks towards me and just embraces me in a giant hug.View image in fullscreenMick Fanning, left, hugs US surfer Kelly Slater after the shark scare.Photograph: Kirstin Scholtz/AFP/Getty ImagesI walk downstairs surrounded by security. Parko is standing at the bottom with Ace and Bec, his wife. Bec’s emotional – she knows how bad it could’ve been. She hugs me and my legs just buckle. That’s when it all sinks in and I’m overcome. I burst into tears as reality hits like a tsunami.Ronnie notices me crumble. “Righto mate, we better get you out of here now.”This is an edited extract from All Heart byMick Fanning(A$36.99, Simon & Schuster)Explore more on these topicsMick FanningSharksSurfingAustralia sportfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Spectre of ghost football hangs over Manchester City win of unknown significance | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Football felt secondary on the first weekend of action since club were found guilty of breaking financial rules
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Football felt secondary on the first weekend of action since club were found guilty of breaking financial rules
Content: Manchester City fans wave inflatable bananas after Erling Haaland had given their side the lead at Anfield.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersView image in fullscreenManchester City fans wave inflatable bananas after Erling Haaland had given their side the lead at Anfield.Photograph: Phil Noble/ReutersPremier LeagueAnalysisSpectre of ghost football hangs over Manchester City win of unknown significanceJonathan WilsonFootball felt secondary on the first weekend of action since club were found guilty of breaking financial rulesSun 11 Oct 2026 15.11 EDTFirst published on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.00 EDTShareThe Cimbri are heading menacingly south, but in Rome life goes on. The asteroid is definitely coming this way, but people go to work, eat, drink, plan as usual. The White Walkers are approaching the Wall, but the squabbles between the great houses go on. Everyone in thePremier Leagueknows the crisis is approaching, thinks – hopes, fears? – it may be apocalyptic, but until it arrives, what can you do but carry on?After any break, there’s always an awkward moment while everybody resets. What was the cliffhanger we left the soap opera on? What new plotline had just been seeded? This is one of the reasons international weeks are so disruptive. It’s not just that the Premier League story slows for a while, it’s that we are reminded that these entities are not eternal but alliances of convenience between paid employees who have a life outside the soap opera.Cherki cracker caps Manchester City win at Liverpool in face of Anfield tauntsRead moreBut there has never before been an international break so disruptive as this, never such a sense of unreality about a weekend of Premier League football. It’s not that, the 2022 World Cup aside, this has been the longest international break in history. Nor can anyone, surely, be unaware of the dominant narrative of this window: between 2009 and 2018,Manchester Citycheated. Perhaps an away game at Anfield for City is not quite the event it was when Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp were at their peak, but it should still be a great footballing occasion. Yet this was an afternoon when the football felt secondary.City continue to protest their innocence, clinging to the now-familiar formula that they have a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that will somehow clear their name, if only people wouldn’t keep refuting it. They havelaunched an appeal, but if that fails the sanction is likely to be unprecedentedly severe. Do their games matter? Will they be annulled before the season’s end? Was this victory just the difference between finishing the season on -100 points and -97? Could they be expelled from the league? Until sentence is announced, there will an air of provisionality about everything they do. It’s the seconds after an incident that everybody knows VAR will check, the ghost football that might be cancelled, but extended for weeks.This, though, is not only an issue of the present; it’s an issue of the past. The sanction may or may not strip City of their titles. Many City fans will ignore such a punishment, continue to claim those honours, will point out that memories cannot be so easily extinguished. But even if City’s appeal is successful, or even if the sanction does not relitigate the past, there will be asterisks there in the minds of those who are not City fans, and perhaps also in the minds of some of those who are. Add inChelsea’s offences, and the Premier League is coming to the end of an 18-year period in which very little was quite as it seemed.View image in fullscreenManchester City fans remain defiant despite the guilty verdict against the club they support.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesTheinflatable bananas brandished by City’s supportat Anfield on Sunday may have harked back to an earlier, more innocent era, but there is no going back. City are not the club of Imre Varadi any more; as it stands they are the clubguilty of the greatest act of cheatingin English football history. Their fans can do the Poznan in a spirit of resistance, but they cannot turn their back on the shame their leaders have brought upon them.What that means for the longer-term credibility of the league can only be guessed at. The basis of sport is faith. Incredible finishes mean little if nothing can be believed. Why go through the emotional agonies if a result might be struck off a decade later for offences committed in the air-conditioned offices of a distant state? Will the City decision undermine faith, or reaffirm it, come as proof that cheats do not prosper, that they will – eventually – be exposed, that the Premier League, almost alone in this grubby world of compromise with and abasement before the mega-rich, is prepared to do what is right?skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionCity were booed, there were some chants of “going down” and there were a handful of banners, but Anfield was not the seething pit of disgust many had anticipated. Nor was there much City-related fury at other grounds, although Manchester United fans, erasing all the silverware of the past 15 years, reinstituted their counter on the Stretford End recording the length of time since City last won a trophy. The general sense is of bafflement and bewilderment; what does this mean? What might happen?It is as though the scale of City’s offences have not yet been fully grasped, that no one quite knows what might happen next. City fans, similarly, seem set on a policy of defiance, as though the scandal is something that has been done to them, rather than the result of the actions of their own directors. To an extent, that is understandable. Until the sanctions are announced, until the result of the appeal is known, the sense of unreality, the phoney war, will go on. The crisis is coming, but its impact has not yet been felt.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueManchester CityFootball politicsanalysisShareReuse this content

title: ‘We make our own noise’: Maresca hails Manchester City after Liverpool triumph | Premier League | The Guardian
description: The head coach said after the 3-0 win at Liverpool, the first game since City’s guilty verdict: ‘You cannot imagine how happy I am. I’m here to win’
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: The head coach said after the 3-0 win at Liverpool, the first game since City’s guilty verdict: ‘You cannot imagine how happy I am. I’m here to win’
Content: Enzo Maresca said: ‘My message to the players has been clear: the noise will always be there so it’s about how we deal with it.’Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca said: ‘My message to the players has been clear: the noise will always be there so it’s about how we deal with it.’Photograph: Paul Ellis/AFP/Getty ImagesPremier League‘We make our own noise’: Maresca hails Manchester City after Liverpool triumph‘You cannot imagine how happy I am … I’m here to win’City win 3-0 at Anfield in first game since guilty verdictAndy Hunterat AnfieldSun 11 Oct 2026 15.43 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.54 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Maresca praised Manchester City for “making their own noise” at Liverpool as they brushed aside the controversy and threats surrounding the club with acomprehensive 3-0 winat Anfield.City, intheir first outingsince the club were found guilty on 114 charges relating to Premier League financial rules, maintained their 100% start to the season courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland, the excellent Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki. A sixth successive league win ensured Maresca equalled the best start to a managerial reign in Premier League history and kept City at the top of the table.Premier League returns in shadow of Manchester City’s judgment day | Jonathan WilsonRead moreThe City head coach said: “My message to the players since we were together three days ago, when they all came back from their national teams, has been quite clear: guys, the noise will always be there so it’s about how we learn to deal with the noise and it’s our duty to make our noise. Our noise is to win games in the way we did today and to be happy. It was our fans making the noise at the end of the game today.”Maresca smiled when asked whether he needed City’s appeal to be heard as quickly as possible in order to celebrate such an impressive win. “You cannot imagine how happy I am,” he replied. “I don’t care. I’m here to try and prepare games and to win games. Hopefully I can speak about this situation when we win the appeal.”City’s chief executive Ferran Soriano was present at Anfield as the fallout from the club’s guilty verdict continues. Maresca reflected: “We were all together. For the importance of the game,Liverpoolaway, Anfield away, it was a good idea from the club to be all together. That togetherness is what we need.”The game turned on the 62nd-minute dismissal of Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch for a second bookable offence. Haaland opened the scoring one minute later and City then ran riot.Andoni Iraola, the Liverpool head coach, said: “We played two different games: one until the red card, and one from the red card until the end. I think we were the better team until the red card and they were better than us, obviously, after the red card. But I think the players deserve credit today because they’ve given everything.”Iraola insisted Gravenberch’s red card was harsh. “I think the first foul of Ryan is never a yellow card, never,” he added. “The referee doesn’t even call the foul straight away. He lets it go, Elliot Anderson does a couple of steps and then decides to go down. I don’t know why he shows the yellow card after that because it’s not a situation where it leaves an advantage.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueEnzo MarescaManchester CityLiverpoolnewsShareReuse this content

title: Impervious Manchester City shrug off chaos and controversy to silence Anfield | Premier League | The Guardian
description: What had been billed as a day of reckoning for the embattled Premier League champions turned into a Sunday afternoon stroll
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: What had been billed as a day of reckoning for the embattled Premier League champions turned into a Sunday afternoon stroll
Content: Banners underlining the level of feeling among Liverpool fans towards Manchester City were dotted around Anfield.Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenBanners underlining the level of feeling among Liverpool fans towards Manchester City were dotted around Anfield.Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueAnalysisImpervious Manchester City shrug off chaos and controversy to silence AnfieldAndy Hunterat AnfieldWhat had been billed as a day of reckoning for the Premier League champions turned into a Sunday afternoon strollSun 11 Oct 2026 16.02 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 17.40 EDTShareAnfield welcomed Manchester City to their new reality, a sullied place where every touch is accompanied by cries of “cheat”, any favourable decision is considered proof of further conspiracy and every victory hollow. But Welcome to Hell this was not. The only body of irrefutable evidence in City’s favoursince the guilty verdicts landedis that Enzo Maresca’s league leaders appear immune to prosecution and persecution.That may well change depending on the outcome of City’s appeal and any punishment that eventually arises, likewise the merits and value of acommanding 3-0 winon Liverpool soil. The sight of Erling Haaland savouring a statement victory in front of City’s supporters after the final whistle, while chants of “going down” echoed around the rest of the stadium, captured the schism at the heart of this Premier League season.Liverpool 0-3 Manchester City: Premier League – as it happenedRead moreCity were transformed by the introduction of Jérémy Doku and the dismissal of the Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch. They were never intimidated, always composed and look a genuine threat to Arsenal’s defence of the title. And yet this could prove their lastPremier Leagueappearance at Anfield for the foreseeable future.It may be difficult, nigh on impossible, to sustain this level of motivation and desire knowing that relegation beckons. Knowing that no one outside City will give them credit for another title triumph did not affect them here, however.In the 17 days since news of City’s guilt first emerged, and the gestation period of a prolonged international break, their return to action in a Premier League undermined and distorted by their 114 breaches had been built up as a chastening day of reckoning for Maresca’s side. It proved nothing of the sort.Anfield can still make its voice heard to seismic effect and in the frantic start whenLiverpoolflew at City, with a fired-up Ronald Araújo whipping up the crowd after winning a challenge against Antoine Semenyo, the collective sense of injustice at a club pipped three times to the title by those in sky blue inspired Andoni Iraola’s players. But bear pits rarely feature in the corporate packaged world of Premier League entertainment 2026.The “reception committee” for the City team coach before the game was populated by fans carrying selfie-sticks and club shop carrier bags, not an incensed brooding mob. At half-time the Kop was asked to cheer on corporate guests of the club sponsor Standard Chartered as they took part in a penalty shootout, many clearly kicking a ball for the first time in their lives.There were incessant chants of “you cheating bastards” and various banners of damning judgement, many with an Oasis twist that may have been appreciated by Noel Gallagher in the away end. “And after all you really robbed us all” read one. “All of your stars are fading away,” read another. “A generation of supporters cheated,” cut to the heart of the issue confronting not only Liverpool but the Premier League itself.View image in fullscreenLiverpool supporters point out that their side finished second to Manchester City three times in the space of eight years.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAThe City support responded in kind. “In Khaldoon we trust – we’ve won it all!” proclaimed the away flags. The visitors, while performing the Poznan before kick-off, also reclaimed one of the “Cheat” flags that had been doing a healthy trade outside the ground before the game. The inflatable bananas that were once part of the City fanscape also made a comeback, a throwback to more innocent days when their club was not in the dock for inflating sponsorship deals. There was more bickering than tangible animosity. The four men who walked on to the pitch carrying the Premier League hoardings before kick-off received a more hostile reception than City’s players when they appeared for the warm-up.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe decision for City’s team coach to arrive by a different route ensured a tame reception for the visitors. All eyes were on the usual entrance on Anfield Road as City were ushered in from the opposite side of the stadium. It meant even the referees’ chief Howard Webb could walk in almost unnoticed. The hostility cranked up as soon as the contest started and City, using their vast experience to telling effect, gradually drained the venom from the atmosphere and the threat from a depleted Liverpool team. But it was the 62nd-minute dismissal of Gravenberch that had the greater bearing on the outcome.Doku proved a devastating substitute for Iliman Ndiaye and tormented Liverpool from the left, being involved not only in the red card but all three City goals. The hosts, minus their two most potent attacking players this season in Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak, plus a hamstrung Dominik Szoboszlai, had no answer with Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola largely anonymous.The Kop made no calls to be handed the trophies lost to City – and what would that really mean now anyway? – but took solace in demanding that punishment be served in the form of relegation this season. “No trophies for 50 years, que será, será,” the home crowd chanted. But there was no immediate retribution for Liverpool here. City dealt with the chaos and the controversy serenely.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueManchester CityLiverpoolanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Pino finishes off Nottingham Forest on Glasner’s unhappy Crystal Palace return | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Selhurst Park offered their returning former manager a generous reception but their team was not as welcoming as Crystal Palace beat Nottingham Forest 3-1
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Selhurst Park offered their returning former manager a generous reception but their team was not as welcoming as Crystal Palace beat Nottingham Forest 3-1
Content: Yéremy Pino gets a bear hug from Jørgen Strand Larsen after scoring Crystal Palace’s third goal.Photograph: Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenYéremy Pino gets a bear hug from Jørgen Strand Larsen after scoring Crystal Palace’s third goal.Photograph: Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesPremier LeaguePino finishes off Nottingham Forest on Glasner’s unhappy Crystal Palace returnEd Aaronsat Selhurst ParkSun 11 Oct 2026 11.28 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt is fair to say Oliver Glasner has had more enjoyable afternoons. TheNottingham Foresthead coach arrived in south London dressed like a bouncer from All Bar One in a black bomber jacket, as if he was anticipating trouble, but was instead given a rapturous reception by the home fans who used to worship him.The generosity towards their former manager seemed to have extended to Palace’s players as Dan Ndoye was handed a goal in the third minute. Pierre Sage’s side were awful in the opening 40 minutes. Yet Forest could not find a way to beat Walter Benítez again as Liam Delap missed a golden chance to extend their lead and the Argentina goalkeeper’s heroics inspired a thrilling comeback that secured Sage’s first home victory in thePremier Leaguesince taking over from Glasner in the summer.Mohamed Belloumi grabs point for Hull in seesaw draw with EvertonRead moreThe irony that Daichi Kamada, who won the Europa League under Glasner while they were at Eintracht Frankfurt before he brought him to Selhurst Park on a free transfer, should score his first Premier League goal to equalise in his 68th appearance was surely not lost on the Austrian.But he and the notoriously trigger-happy Evangelos Marinakis – the Forest owner who was conspicuous by his absence from the directors’ box after his public spats with his Palace counterpart, Steve Parish – will have serious concerns about how his team capitulated after conceding the equaliser. Jefferson Lerma bundled home the second from a corner just before half-time and Yéremy Pino wrapped up the points with a goal that was greeted with a chorus of: “You’re getting sacked in the morning”, directed towards Glasner.“Call it karma or whatever but it was like I didn’t deserve to win at Selhurst Park because the players did everything,” said Glasner, who claimed not to have heard the taunts from the Palace fans. “I think this was the most dominant Nottingham Forest performance. But not the right result. So, this gives me confidence. My job is not to be influenced negatively by the result.”There has been plenty of water under the bridge since these two sides met here 14 months ago. Marinakis is suing Palace and “persons unknown” after a banner featuring an incendiary cartoon of him was unfurled during the first half of that game, with the supporters’ group that is thought to have been behind it having since disbanded. Glasner’s decision to join Forest in the summer only added to the ill-feeling that was created by the dispute over Palace’s demotion from the Europa League last season, even if the Austrian was given a warm welcome before and after the game.The home fans made it clear where their grievances remain as they immediately launched into the anti-Uefa and Marinakis song that was the soundtrack totheir Conference League triumphunder Glasner, while the Forest supporters responded with taunts of: “We’ve got Ollie Glasner”. They had more reason to celebrate after only two minutes when Anan Khalaili’s weak header presented Ndoye with the chance to run through and score. Forest could barely believe their luck.View image in fullscreenThe Nottingham Forest head coach, Oliver Glasner, responds to a generous reception from the Crystal Palace supporters.Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/ReutersThey piled on the pressure, with makeshift defender Lerma – only playing in the absence of the suspended Axel Disasi – looking particularly vulnerable. Jaydee Canvot was guilty of losing possession when Morgan Gibbs-White picked out the unmarked Ndoye and Benítez tipped over before Daniel Muñoz was inches away from scoring against his former club.But the momentum shifted firmly towards the hosts thanks to a miraculous save from Benítez – deputising for the injured Dean Henderson – that denied Delap from three yards out after Gibbs-White’s shot rebound off the crossbar. “Walter made a save with a lot of bravery,” said Sage, who refused the opportunity to gloat about beating Glasner. “It’s not about revenge,” he insisted.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDelap spurned another golden opportunity with his head and Forest were made to pay just before the break when Kamada scrambled home inside the six-yard area after Jørgen Strand Larsen’s pass deflected straight into his path. Suddenly Palace found their belief. Tyrick Mitchell’s volley was tipped over and from the resulting corner Lerma leapt highest and the ball squirmed through the legs of Matz Sels and just over the line. Replays suggested that Lerma’s effort grazed the arm of team-mate Khalaili on its way in, but VAR let the matter go.One characteristic Sage has inherited is his team’s difficulty in defending set pieces and Palace were lucky to escape when a header from Gibbs-White at the start of the second half was deflected on to the post by Mitchell. Forest looked at sixes and sevens at the other end when Lerma again caused chaos from a corner but they scrambled the ball away.There was no such reprieve a few minutes later when Quinten Timber’s pass was diverted into the path of Strand Larsen and Pino made no mistake with the rebound. The Spain forward then turned provider but Strand Larsen could not find a way past Sels. That didn’t stop the Palace fans from gleefully asking Glasner what the score was. Ndoye and Neco Williams had chances to make things interesting late on but Forest – and Glasner – had been humbled by then.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueCrystal PalaceNottingham Forestmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Mohamed Belloumi grabs point for Hull in seesaw draw with Everton | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Mohamed Belloumi scored Hull’s equaliser in a 2-2 draw with Everton, in which both sides led in the second half
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Mohamed Belloumi scored Hull’s equaliser in a 2-2 draw with Everton, in which both sides led in the second half
Content: Mohamed Belloumi shows his delight after equalising.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/SportsphotoView image in fullscreenMohamed Belloumi shows his delight after equalising.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/SportsphotoPremier LeagueMohamed Belloumi grabs point for Hull in seesaw draw with EvertonPress AssociationSun 11 Oct 2026 11.13 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHull retained their unbeaten home record since returning to thePremier Leaguewith an entertaining draw against Everton at the MKM Stadium.Brennan Johnson found the net in the 34th minute but was denied a first Premier League goal forEvertonfollowing a video assistant referee check, leaving the sides to go in goalless at the break. The hosts wasted little time after the interval, however, as Joe Gelhardt opened the scoring in the 48th minute following an error by Ainsley Maitland-Niles.Pino finishes off Nottingham Forest on Glasner’s unhappy Crystal Palace returnRead moreKiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised for Everton seven minutes later, and Thierno Barry, who had squandered plenty of earlier chances, then put the visitors ahead midway through the second period. Hull responded swiftly, though, with the substitute Mohamed Belloumi pulling the home team level in the 74th minute.The Tigers have returned to the top flight with an unexpected bang, tasting defeat for the first time in their final fixture before the international break at Newcastle. They were slow off the mark in the early exchanges here, but eventually produced a forward burst of play that saw both Oli McBurnie and then Lewie Coyle threaten before being thwarted.Gelhardt caused danger with a run down the right in the 22nd minute but his shot was comfortably collected by Jordan Pickford. Matt Crooks got his head to a corner 10 minutes later, but James Tarkowski cleared and play sped to the opposite end.Barry unleashed a shot that was gathered by Konstantinos Tzolakis, but the ball rolled from his hands and was fired in by Johnson for what appeared to be the opener 11 minutes before half-time. But, after a lengthy VAR check, the winger was ruled offside. Gelhardt and Nobel Mendy then went close to easing the nerves of home fans with near-misses before half-time.The hosts did not have to wait long for the opener after the break though. Sorba Thomas capitalised on a mistake from Maitland-Niles and fed Gelhardt, who coolly nudged the ball beyond Pickford in the 48th minute.The Everton response was fairly rapid, however, and Maitland-Niles atoned for his slip-up by finding Dewsbury-Hall, who headed home in the 55th minute.View image in fullscreenKiernan Dewsbury-Hall heads home to make it 1-1.Photograph: Lee Parker/CameraSport/Getty ImagesBarry, who had much to ponder after missing two earlier chances, then redeemed himself when he pounced to lash beyond Tzolakis to put the visitors ahead for the first time in the match.But Hull, who had made a handful of changes, were not behind for long as the substitutes Elliot Stroud and Belloumi linked up and the latter sent a left-footed shot past Pickford in the 74th minute to secure a point for the Tigers.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDavid Moyes felt his Everton squad completely underperformed. Change is afoot at the club after it was announced earlier in the weekthey would be put up for sale, but their manager was in no mood for excuses after the draw.He said: “I’m really disappointed that we didn’t come away with three points, I couldn’t see them getting a goal when we went 2-1 up – I thought if anything we would go on and finish it. It looked really unlike us, the way we gave the goals away today, it was very, very poor.“Hull have had some great results here, against Manchester United and Villa, they’re not easy to beat and they weren’t [today] but I thought we should have gone on and won the game comfortably.“The overall performance from everyone was so far below our level, way below where we should be. I’m not giving the players any room for excuses because of what’s going on, whether that be the transfer window or that be ownership.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueHull CityEvertonmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: European football: Freiburg move top of Bundesliga while Isco keeps Betis flying high | European club football | The Guardian
description: Keisuke Goto sealed a late 2-1 win over Schalke for 10-man Freiburg while Lazio joined Inter at the top of Serie A as Roma were held at Como
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Keisuke Goto sealed a late 2-1 win over Schalke for 10-man Freiburg while Lazio joined Inter at the top of Serie A as Roma were held at Como
Content: Keisuke Goto heads in to seal Freiburg’s 2-1 win against Schalke.Photograph: Tom Weller/DPA/APView image in fullscreenKeisuke Goto heads in to seal Freiburg’s 2-1 win against Schalke.Photograph: Tom Weller/DPA/APEuropean club footballEuropean football: Freiburg move top of Bundesliga while Isco keeps Betis flying highGoto seals late 2-1 win over Schalke for 10-man FreiburgLazio join Inter at top of Serie A as Roma held at ComoGuardian sportand agenciesSun 11 Oct 2026 17.15 EDTFirst published on Sun 11 Oct 2026 12.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTen-manFreiburgscored an 85th-minute winner ⁠through Keisuke Goto to snatch a 2-1 home victory over ⁠Schalke 04⁠on ​Sunday and move top of the Bundesliga.Freiburg, who had ⁠already made a club-record start with 10 points from their opening ⁠four matches, climbed to 13 points, ​ahead of Borussia ‌Dortmund on ‌goal difference. The champions, Bayern Munich, who drew 2-2 ‌against Augsburg on Saturday, are third on 11.European football: Gordon boosts Barcelona, Neuer errors cost Bayern in drawRead moreWith Freiburg in control, Maximilian Eggestein put the hosts in front after 10 minutes, butSchalkehit ‌back through Adrian Gantenbein on the half-hour. Freiburg were reduced to ​10 men when Yuito Suzuki received a second yellow card in the 64th minute, seemingly handing Schalke the initiative.But ⁠the visitors were far too passive and ​toothless ​in attack to ​make the extra man count ​and Freiburg ‌punished them ​five ​minutes before the end with the Japan international Goto snatching the winner with a glancing header.Borussia Mönchengladbachremained rock bottom of the Bundesliga after a 2-1 defeat to local rivalsCologneon Sunday, in a match overshadowed by ugly scenes on the terraces.The game was suspended for several minutes and riot police surrounded the away block after Gladbach fans appeared to fire fireworks into the home sections after Said El Mala’s superb second-half winner. That maintained pointless Gladbach’s miserable start to the season as the new coach, Alexander Blessin, failed to prevent the club falling to their fifth defeat in as many games.TheReal Betisplaymaker Isco scored in each half ⁠as his side breezed to a 5-2 home win overOsasunaon ⁠Sunday that lifts ⁠them ​to third place in La Liga, five points behind the leaders, Barcelona, and one ahead ⁠of Real Madrid.Isco fired home from the penalty spot in the 10th minute to ⁠open the scoring, and Abde Ezzalzouli added a second ​before the break after ‌Betis won the ‌ball high up the pitch and countered quickly.Betis ‌looked to be set for a comfortable afternoon when Diego Llorente added a third three minutes after half-time, but two quick goals for the visitors from Ante Budimir and Raúl García reduced the ‌deficit to 3-2 in the 56th minute.However, Isco eased their nerves again when he ​snapped up a loose ball in the box and rifled it home, and José Antonio Morante came off the bench in the 90th minute before scoring deep ⁠into stoppage time to leave Betis on 19 ​points after ​eight games.Earlier on ​Sunday,Real Sociedadheld off a spirited ​comeback from ‌Deportivo La Coruña​to ​emerge with a 3-2 win at home, while strugglingElchegrabbed a much-needed point by holding visitorsCelta Vigoto a scoreless draw.Laziomoved level on points with Inter at the top ofSerie Awith a 3-1 win overMonzaon Sunday as 10-manRomaplayed out the first goalless draw of the Italian season atComo.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenNuno Tavares gives Lazio an early lead.Photograph: Riccardo Antimiani/EPAUnder Gennaro Gattuso, who has bounced back after his failure in charge of the Italian national side that missed out on the 2026 World Cup,Laziocontinued their strong start to the season. Still unbeaten, the Roman side secured a fifth victory in six matches to pull level on 16 points with Inter, who beat Parma 3-0 at San Siro on Saturday.Nuno Tavares gave Lazio a third-minute lead and Gustav Isaksen doubled it midway through the first half. Monza had Lorenzo Lucchesi sent off on 35 minutes for hauling down Tijjani Noslin as he broke through on goal, but the 16th-placed visitors rattled Lazio after the break, pulling a goal back and coming close to equalising before conceding a third goal in the closing stages.Roma left Como frustrated. The dismissal of league top scorer Donyell Malen for a dangerous tackle early in the second half forced them to scale back their ambitions. Neither team could find the breakthrough in a clash between two sides widely regarded as dark horses for the title, leaving Inter and Lazio two points clear ofRomaafter their respective wins over Parma and Monza.Bolognapicked up their first win of the season by beatingLecce2-1.Milanremain unbeaten in Serie A after drawing 1-1 withSassuolo. Adrien Rabiot’s opener was cancelled out by Cas Odenthal as Milan settled for their third draw of the campaign and stay fifth in the table.Juventusare one point behind Milan after an 81st minute equaliser from Randal Kolo Muani salvaged a 1-1 draw with fourth-placedCagliari.Marseilleput an end to their four-game losing run in Ligue 1 as Amine Harit and Himad Abdelli scored in a 2-0 win atTroyes. StrugglingMarseillebegan the weekend in the relegation zone after suffering five losses in a row in all competitions, but a pair of second-half goals lifted them to 13th place.Harit steered in a cross from Emerson Palmieri shortly after half-time before Abdelli converted a late penalty as Marseille avoided matching their worst losing streak over the past 40 years. Troyes had gone close to an equaliser just before Abdelli made the points safe for Marseille, but Renaud Ripart’s stoppage-time volley crashed against the post.Rennesmoved up to third earlier in the day with a 4-1 win againstAuxerre, whileNicecame from behind to beatStrasbourg2-1.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballSerie AComoRomaMarseilleFreiburgSchalkenewsShareReuse this content

title: Joy for Eckert as 10-man Southampton edge out Portsmouth in feisty derby | Championship | The Guardian
description: James Bree’s first-half goal proved the difference as Southampton beat Portsmouth 1-0 despite Cameron Bragg’s red card just before half-time
Author: Billy Munday
Headline: James Bree’s first-half goal proved the difference as Southampton beat Portsmouth 1-0 despite Cameron Bragg’s red card just before half-time
Content: Tonda Eckert screams in delight at the final whistle.Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTonda Eckert screams in delight at the final whistle.Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty ImagesChampionshipJoy for Eckert as 10-man Southampton edge out Portsmouth in feisty derbyBilly MundaySun 11 Oct 2026 09.18 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt the full-time whistle in the south coast derby, Tonda Eckert thrust his arms out wide and roared into the sky with the rest of the Southampton supporters. It had been a tense 90 minutes after a tense few months, but finally the young German coach could let it all out. At the end of a week where he found out that he will faceno immediate banfor his part in the Spygate scandal that rocked the Championship last season, he helped deliver Southampton’s first home win over Portsmouth for 22 years.Championship roundup: Swansea fight back to beat Norwich; Middlesbrough go secondRead moreSouthampton played more than half of a fiercely contested game with 10 men after Cameron Bragg was sent off for a second yellow card on 44 minutes and Eckert was keen to divert credit elsewhere at full time. “I think that one today belongs to the players,” he said. “If you go a man down there’s not so much you can do as a manager outside of trying to give a structure that helps. It’s the players that dig out games like this.”There was widespread surprise at the leniency of the punishment that allowed Eckert to take his seat in the dugout for the derby. After Southamptonadmitted to spying on three opponents last season, the 33-year-old was handed a six-week ban, suspended until the end of the 2027-28 campaign, and a £28,000 fine for misconduct.An FA independent disciplinary commission noted Eckert’s “genuine contrition” at what had happened. At Southampton, there is a sense that their expulsion from the playoffs in May and subsequent four-point deduction was punishment enough, and Eckert is keen to move on from a period of uncertainty that he admitted this week had changed his life.This win was evidence of a club sticking together. James Bree was the author of the winning goal, turning the ball home after 20 minutes, but the pattern of the game shifted with Bragg’s dismissal. Southampton, united and resolute, held on to move into the top half – they would be third without the points deduction – with Eckert now able to contemplate another promotion push.View image in fullscreenSouthampton’s James Bree coolly opens the scoring, his goal turning out to be the winner.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAPortsmouth were as usual given a pre-match police escort to St Mary’s and their full-back Jayden Meghoma, who made his professional debut for Southampton as a 17-year-old, was a magnet for Saints ire. He was a threat down the left, firing wide at the near post in a promising opening, but he lost Bree for the goal. Finn Azaz was given too much space in midfield and clipped a ball in behind a static Meghoma for Bree, forward from right-back, to guide a left-footed finish into the far corner.Ebou Adams, who scored Portsmouth’s equaliser in a 1-1 draw in this fixture in January, was a central figure early on. He twice picked Bragg’s pocket in the Southampton half and drew yellow cards on both occasions. Bragg was consoled by his teammates after seeing red for an instinctive tug of Adams’s shirt after being caught on the ball.The decision to start Bragg in a holding midfield role had backfired. “It will be a learning [curve] for him, but I asked him to be brave,” Eckert said. “I asked him to get on the ball and he does just that. I’ll take that on me, then.”View image in fullscreenCam Bragg is consoled as he walks off the pitch.Photograph: Robin Jones/Getty ImagesColby Bishop, whose header was well saved by Daniel Peretz, and Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, who drilled a shot just wide, went close to equalising before Eckert could try to plug the gaps at half-time.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe game was just as frantic after the break. Azaz was perhaps lucky not to be sent off for a wild lunge on Adams. When Bree was treated for a battle scar around his eye, Eckert held council with his remaining midfielders James Ward-Prowse and Flynn Downes as Pompey continued to knock on the door. The substitute Adrian Segecic was drifting into spaces and had fizzed a couple of low efforts wide in the minutes before, while the right-back Zak Swanson saw his cut-back cleared by Jack Stephens from under the Southampton crossbar.View image in fullscreenTempers fray at St Mary’s but the hosts held on for victory.Photograph: Warren Little/Getty Images“It was a different game after the red card,” said the Portsmouth head coach, John Mousinho. “But for the amount of pressure that we had in the second half, the amount of opportunities we had, to not put the ball in the back of the net – we’re devastated.”While Eckert gradually cut back his side’s attacking presence, Mousinho emptied his bench in an attempt to find a way through a Southampton defence marshalled by Stephens and Keven Schlotterbeck, who laid their bodies on the line more than once in front of Peretz. Their clean sheet was a priceless end to a week where their manager was given something of a clean slate.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipSouthamptonPortsmouthmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic end losing skid and take top spot back from Rangers | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Jota made his long-awaited return to action as Celtic claimed a much-needed 2-0 victory at Motherwell to move top of the Premiership again
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Jota made his long-awaited return to action as Celtic claimed a much-needed 2-0 victory at Motherwell to move top of the Premiership again
Content: Celtic’s Camilo Durán (centre) celebrates after he opened the scoring at Motherwell.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAView image in fullscreenCeltic’s Camilo Durán (centre) celebrates after he opened the scoring at Motherwell.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PAScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Celtic end losing skid and take top spot back from RangersBhoys on top of table, while Rangers beat Kilmarnock 3-1Calvin Miller scores two penalties in Hearts 5-0 St MirrenPress AssociationSun 11 Oct 2026 12.20 EDTFirst published on Sat 10 Oct 2026 12.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJota made his long-awaited return to action asCelticclaimed a much-needed 2-0 victory atMotherwellto move top of the Premiership again and ease the sense of gloom and tension that had engulfed the club during the international break.Five months on from a dramatic late win that helped them on their way to last season’s title, Martin O’Neill’s side enjoyed another big result at Fir Park to end a three-game losing streak and climb back ahead ofRangers, who had leapfrogged them at the summit on Saturday.European football: Lazio join Inter at top of Serie A as Roma held at ComoRead moreAfter a renewal of hostilities between supporters and the Celtic board as well as uncertainty about O’Neill’s future as manager during the three-week break since theirhome defeat by their bitter rivals, an early strike from Camilo Durán helped restore a semblance of calm for the Hoops.The champions had control of proceedings thereafter and – despite an inspired display from the home goalkeeper Alex Paulsen – Celtic added to their lead through Benjamin Nygren in the 58th minute as they made it seven wins in eight league matches this term.The huge Hoops support sporadically unfurled banners and chanted against the club’s major shareholder Dermot Desmond, who was the subject ofa tennis-ball protestby a group of balaclava-clad supporters at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews last weekend. Long before the end of a largely one-sided encounter, however, it was Motherwell’s fans who were displaying their frustration by making for the exits as their insipid side slid to a fourth consecutive defeat.“If we’d been beaten today, of course, that would have been four on the trot, so that doesn’t help any manager,” said O’Neill. “But we didn’t. For us to get on track again domestically was delightful.”Derek McInnes praised his Rangers players and blamed the extended international break for some disjointed play in Saturday’s 3-1 win overKilmarnock.Rangers went into the break three up at Ibrox after Ryan Naderi twice headed home either side of a Kevin Kelsy strike. But Killie had chances throughout, especially after the interval, before finally getting their reward when the substitute Nicky Clescenco struck on a last-minute counterattack. The visitors ended the game with six efforts on target to Rangers’ four, but the home goalkeeper, Ivor Pandur, was seriously troubled only once before being beaten.View image in fullscreenRyan Naderi celebrates after opening the scoring for Rangers against Kilarnock.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA“I was really pleased with how clinical we were in the first half,” said McInnes. “We put the ball in the box, we scored goals. We just didn’t do it enough for whatever reason. But we have to be honest, for long spells we looked like a team that hadn’t been together for the last three weeks. There’s a bit of understanding for me where the players have been. Whoever came up with this idea, it’s such a long time for your players to be away. We pay their wages, we look after our players and for them to be away for nearly three weeks is too long. But we’ve got the job done and credit the players for digging deep and getting three points.”Heartseased to their biggest home win in the league for three-and-a-half years as they dismantledSt Mirren5-0 to remain on the coattails of Rangers and Celtic.Third-placed Hearts dominated from the start and Laurent Mendy fired them ahead in the 20th minute. Calvin Miller scored two penalties, either side of half-time, before goals from Cláudio Braga and Josh McPake ensured a smooth afternoon for Hearts.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenHearts’ Calvin Miller scores his side’s second from the spot against St Mirren.Photograph: Zak Mauger/Getty ImagesIt was Hearts’ biggest league win at Tynecastle since they defeated Ross County 6-1 under Steven Naismith in April 2023 and they are now comfortably the top scorers in the league. Hearts’ manager, Wouter Vrancken, said: “We try to play a kind of football that is positive and constructive and proactive, and not a reaction. I think people come to the stadium to see nice football, to see goals from your side.”Josh Fowler’s first-half penalty earnedSt Johnstonea 1-0 win overAberdeenputting them into the top five. Fowler’s spot-kick, awarded against Jack Milne after a lengthy video assistant referee check, proved the only goal of the game as the Dons huffed and puffed to no avail in front of goal.Ashley Hay scrambled in a stoppage-time winner to secureDundeea 2-1 victory atFalkirk. The striker, out since early August with a ligament sprain, converted from close range after latching on to Ethan Hamilton’s free-kick in the first minute of added time. His goal completed the turnaround after Owen Bevan’s second goal for the Dark Blues had cancelled out Jacob Murrell’s first-half penalty at Falkirk Stadium.Marink Reedijk endured a disappointing first game asHibernian’s manager as his side suffered a 1-0 defeat againstDundee Unitedat Tannadice. The hosts scored in the first half through winger Daniel Bennie, on loan from QPR, and the visitors finished the game with 10 men after Jacob Devaney was sent off.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipRangersKilmarnocknewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘So, so grateful’: Nathan Cleary confirms reason behind Mary Fowler’s Matildas absence | Matildas | The Guardian
description: The injured NRL star has expressed deep appreciation to his partner, after she flew back to Australia to spend time with him post-surgery
Author: Jack Snape
Headline: The injured NRL star has expressed deep appreciation to his partner, after she flew back to Australia to spend time with him post-surgery
Content: Nathan Cleary posted on social media praising his partner Mary Fowler who returned to Australia to be with him after surgery on both legs.Photograph: Nathan Cleary/InstagramView image in fullscreenNathan Cleary posted on social media praising his partner Mary Fowler who returned to Australia to be with him after surgery on both legs.Photograph: Nathan Cleary/InstagramMatildas‘So, so grateful’: Nathan Cleary confirms reason behind Mary Fowler’s Matildas absenceFowler pulled out of Australia squad for ‘personal reasons’Attacker is now back in Australia with injured NRL star post-surgeryJack SnapeSun 11 Oct 2026 19.38 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 21.40 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleInjured rugby league player Nathan Cleary has expressed deep appreciation toMatildasforward Mary Fowler, his partner who flew to Australia to spend time with him as he recovers from major surgery.Fowler withdrew from international duty with the Australian national team, wholost 4-2 to Germanyin a friendly on Saturday, and has been spending time with Cleary in Sydney.Sam Kerr on target but Matildas outclassed by youthful Germany in European friendlyRead moreHe posted on Instagram on Sunday evening with a series of photos of their time together in recent days.“I simply do not have enough space in this caption for the amount of nice adjectives I would use to describe Mary Fowler but this woman is the absolute best!” he wrote.“I can’t thank you enough for flying to the other side of the world to look after me and be by my side during this past week of recovery. I’m a very lucky man and so, so grateful.”Fowler responded, saying she was “very lucky” and “it’s easy to look after someone when they’re a big cutie patootie”.The Manchester City forward had earlier posted herself with Cleary and his dog Prince while supporting Cleary’s teammate Liam Henry, who was fundraising for Parkinson’s on Saturday.View image in fullscreenCleary and Fowler together in a recent social media post.Photograph: Mary Fowler/InstagramIt confirmed the reason for Fowler’s withdrawal from the Matildas’ squad which had been previouslydescribed as for “personal circumstances”.Matildas coach Joe Montemurro addressed her absence prior to the match in Karlsruhe.“It’s really important that we create an environment that is important for the player, and as the circumstances are private I’m not going to elaborate,” Montemurro said.“But yes, absolutely, discussions were had with Mary, with the club, and with the relative people, and we believe that we’ve made the right decision and I think everyone’s in support of the situation.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toFootball Desk AustraliaSign up for expert analysis from Jonathan Wilson as well as a rundown of Australians playing in the major leaguesEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWithout Fowler in their lineup, the Matildas quickly fell two goals down to Germany in Friday’s match, and despite promise could not complete a comeback despite bringing the score back to 3-2 the latter stages.Midfielder Kyra Cooney-Cross was also left out of the Matildas’ squad for the match as she continues her return to top-flight football after the death of her mother in July.Fowler will also miss the Matildas’ friendly against Haiti this week in France.Clearysuffered a broken left legin Penrith’s NRL preliminary final defeat to Newcastle, and healso underwent surgery on his right footto correct a stress fracture.The 28-year-old requires a wheelchair for his mobility, and Fowler was shown on Instagram helping re-tie his medical boot and massaging his thigh.Manchester City’s next WSL match is in seven days against Brighton.Explore more title: Georgia Voll’s quickfire century lifts Australia to ODI series win against Bangladesh | Australia women's cricket team | The Guardian
description: Opener Georgia Voll smashed her third ODI century in just her 15th match to secure Australia a comfortable nine-wicket win over Bangladesh and a series victory
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Opener Georgia Voll smashed her third ODI century in just her 15th match to secure Australia a comfortable nine-wicket win over Bangladesh and a series victory
Content: Australia’s Georgia Voll celebrates reaching her century in the second women's ODI against Bangladesh at Allan Border Field in Brisbane.Photograph: Darren England/AAPView image in fullscreenAustralia’s Georgia Voll celebrates reaching her century in the second women's ODI against Bangladesh at Allan Border Field in Brisbane.Photograph: Darren England/AAPAustralia women's cricket teamGeorgia Voll’s quickfire century lifts Australia to ODI series win against BangladeshBangladesh 220-6; Australia 221-1 | Australia win by nine wicketsVoll’s unbeaten 131 off 97 helps hosts take unassailable 2-0 series leadAustralian Associated PressSun 11 Oct 2026 17.52 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 19.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOpener Georgia Voll smashed her third ODI century in just her 15th match to secure Australia a comfortable nine-wicket win over Bangladesh and a series victory.Earlier, Bangladesh centurion Sobhana Mostary played one of the great ODI knocks to lift the visitors to 220-6 as records tumbled at Brisbane’s Allan Border Field.Phoebe Litchfield powers Australia to crushing ODI victory over BangladeshRead moreMostary, 24, made a magnificent 118 off 134 deliveries and with her captain Nigar Sultana (74no off 114) added 195 for the fourth wicket – the highest partnership against Australia in women’s ODI history.But making a mockery of the run chase, Voll and Phoebe Litchfield added 162 off just 119 deliveries in an opening stand that combined brute strength and creativity to the maximum, setting Australia up for an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series.Litchfield (70 off 51) played strokes all around the ground in her entertaining knock while Voll’s power game came to the fore as she bludgeoned anything loose. Voll’s unbeaten 131 off 97 deliveries became the highest individual women’s ODI total at the venue, breaking a record Mostary had equalled only hours earlier.The player of the match’s strong bottom hand came to the fore and she was also dominant through cover when given width as Australia coasted to victory in 28.1 overs. Voll, 23, became the first woman to score two ODI centuries at AB Field after making 101 against India at the venue in 2024.“I love batting out there with Phoebe and to have a partnership and get the team off to a good start was the most important thing,” Voll said. “I base my game off a power game and go through the gears. I look to hit the ball hard and straight early and take it on once I get in.”Mostary and Sultana’s stand was the largest for any Bangladesh wicket in women’s ODIs and was the foundation of the team’s highest total against Australia. It was not enough to challenge Australia but it was achieved with immaculate strokeplay, tactical nous and plenty of courage.View image in fullscreenSobhana Mostary acknowledges the crowd after scoring a century.Photograph: Darren England/AAPThe two Bangladesh heroes came together with their side desperate at 8-3 in the eighth over and embarked on their rescue mission with class.Mostary brought up her fifty with a cut shot off legspinner Alana King after driving her through cover with panache to the fence. She earlier struck three exquisite boundaries through the offside in leggie Georgia Wareham’s first over.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMostary now holds the record for the highest all-time score by a No 5 against Australia in women’s ODI history, and the best by a Bangladesh batter.Sultana was strong off her legs, with two immaculate flicks to the fence with perfect balance a highlight. She played the perfect foil to Mostary.Australia quick Megan Schutt (4-36) was the pick of the bowlers, including ending Mostary’s epic knock when she struck her leg stump.Both sides were unchanged from Friday’s opening match of the three-match series, which Australia won by seven wickets.Explore more on these topicsAustralia women's cricket teamBangladesh women's cricket teamWomen's cricketCricketAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Liverpool 0-3 Manchester City: Premier League – as it happened | Premier League | The Guardian
description: City embraced a hostile atmosphere and overwhelmed Liverpool after Ryan Gravenberch’s red card
Author: Rob Smyth
Headline: City embraced a hostile atmosphere and overwhelmed Liverpool after Ryan Gravenberch’s red card
Content: 8h ago13.42 EDTDavid HytnerMatch report: Liverpool 0-3 Manchester CityIt is a soundtrack thatManchester Cityhave heard before but never for such sustained bursts during a match. It came from the Liverpool support, first ringing out around Anfield before kick-off and coming at regular intervals thereafter.It was always going to be like this as City feel their way into a new reality, one conditioned by the guilty verdicts handed to them by an independent commission on virtually all of the 100-plus charges they have faced for breaking the Premier League’s financial rules. City continue to maintain their innocence and have appealed.The Kop wanted to tell City what they are. And where they are going. According to them, they are cheats, who are set to be relegated. It was not exactly a bear-pit of an atmosphere; it was not really intimidating. It was more of an outpouring and it was impossible to ignore.City did not care. They rolled with the invective. And after a slow-burn contest turned on a second yellow card for theLiverpoolmidfielder, Ryan Gravenberch, in the 62nd minute, City cut loose. All that their players can do is blot out the noise. They did so here, running all over Liverpool’s ten men to maintain their 100% start to the Premier League season.Cherki cracker caps Manchester City win at Liverpool in face of Anfield tauntsRead moreShareUpdated at13.52 EDT

title: Kimi Antonelli admits he can taste F1 glory after Verstappen wins Singapore GP | Formula One 2026 | The Guardian
description: Kimi Antonelli could seal the drivers’ title in the next race in Texas after Max Verstappen won the F1 Singapore Grand Prix
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Kimi Antonelli could seal the drivers’ title in the next race in Texas after Max Verstappen won the F1 Singapore Grand Prix
Content: Kimi Antonelli pours champagne over his head on the podium after the Singapore GP.Photograph: Mark Sutton/Formula 1/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKimi Antonelli pours champagne over his head on the podium after the Singapore GP.Photograph: Mark Sutton/Formula 1/Getty ImagesFormula One 2026Kimi Antonelli admits he can taste F1 glory after Verstappen wins Singapore GPItalian can win the title in Texas in late OctoberVerstappen led race at Marina Bay from start to finishGiles RichardsSun 11 Oct 2026 13.41 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 15.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKimi Antonelli said he can finally dare to dream about winning his first Formula One world championship after he finished in third place at the Singapore Grand Prix and put himself in a position where he could secure the title at the next round in Austin.Max Verstappen won with a dominant driveat the Marina Bay circuit but behind him, Antonelli’s podium means he could become F1’s youngest champion at the age of 20, in two weeks’ time. Antonelli leads his Mercedes teammate, George Russell, by 102 points and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton by 111. With six meetings remaining and 25 points for the winner of each race, the Italian will take the title if he wins in Austin and Russell finishes ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower.Resurgent Verstappen holds off Leclerc to seal dominant F1 Singapore GP winRead moreWhen asked if he dared to dream that his childhood ambition of becoming champion was within reach, he acknowledged he did with a smile. “For sure,” he said. “I know it’s very close, I know it’s there but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can. The mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can.”Mercedes were outpaced by Red Bull in Singapore, with the silver arrows still striving to exploit recent upgrades but Antonelli feels he and the team will have more to come in Texas.“This weekend I haven’t particularly driven that well,” he added. “I felt like I could have done a better job but I feel confident that a week to reset and I’m really looking forward to being back in Austin. But at the end of the day, if I don’t do my job well, then the result won’t come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that.”Hamilton, who finished sixth, issued an apology to his Ferrari team after his call to not pit under the virtual safety car proved costly, leaving him vulnerable on worn tyres at the death, where he was passed by three rivals. He was unwell after the race and given leave to miss his media duties but Ferrari issued a comment from the British driver. “A painful lesson today but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made,” the 41-year-old said. “Not every call will work out and I can accept getting it wrong but I’m sorry for the team for the points we lost today.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Ferrari team principal, Fred Vasseur, made it clear the team had not been at fault. “We were P2, P3 on track, we called two of our guys to pit behind the VSC, one of our guys said: ‘No I prefer to stay on track’, or he missed pit entry. Don’t blame the team,” he noted.Explore more on these topicsFormula One 2026Kimi AntonelliFormula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Tension, ‘cheat’ banners and inflatable bananas: Manchester City’s welcome to Anfield | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: A lively atmosphere greeted the former Premier League champions for their first game since being found guilty of breaking financial fair play rules
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: A lively atmosphere greeted the former Premier League champions for their first game since being found guilty of breaking financial fair play rules
Content: Manchester City cheats merchandise is sold outside Anfield ahead of kick-off.Photograph: Matt West/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenManchester City cheats merchandise is sold outside Anfield ahead of kick-off.Photograph: Matt West/ShutterstockLiverpoolTension, ‘cheat’ banners and inflatable bananas: Manchester City’s welcome to AnfieldA lively atmosphere greeted the former Premier League champions for their first game since being found guilty of breaking financial fair play rulesWill Unwinat AnfieldSun 11 Oct 2026 12.50 EDTLast modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 17.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFans lined the streets of Anfield in preparation for the arrival of theManchester Cityteam bus, with pyrotechnics and pure vitriol adding to the tense pre-match atmosphere. Every vantage point was taken, with spectators standing on walls to get a glimpse of the enemy, only for the coach to sneak in from the opposite side of the ground to avoid confrontation.The subterfuge defused a volatile situation that could have turned into an incendiary one. Tensions were high on Merseyside. Since the City takeover in 2008, Liverpool have finished second to their rivals on three occasions, although only one of those falls within the parameters of the investigation intoCity’s financial breaches of Premier League rules. Liverpool supporters are aggrieved, feeling they would have won more trophies had City not circumnavigated the rules to help sign elite players.Premier League returns in shadow of Manchester City’s judgment day | Jonathan WilsonRead moreLiverpool were punished in 2018 aftersupporters launched missiles at the team busas the City players were driven to Anfield for a Champions League clash. The animosity has only been heightened by the independent commission’s guilty verdict.References to the verdict were not difficult to find at stalls outside. For £15 – haggling took it down to £10 – it was possible to buy a “Guilty 114” flag, including an AI image of the City squad in prison uniforms or a “Cheats” banner in the style of the Oasis logo.Many supporters, however, were content with the traditional – and much maligned – half and half scarf to commemorate such an occasion. The fashion-conscious could pick up T-shirts with a similar motif. There were more frugal offerings, with homemade banners carrying the blunt message being paraded around the ground.View image in fullscreenLiverpool supporters lined the streets outside Anfield waiting to greet the Manchester City team coach.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPAThere was a sense of injustice and thousands wanted to express it. A solitary City fan, clad in sky blue, stood among the sea of red. He was unbothered by the commotion around him but was left alone because he is not at fault.Social media chatter suggested City merited a “bus greeting” on Anfield Road and police were prepared for such an eventuality. There was toxicity and hostility on both sides in the buildup, with away supporters chanting their anthem of “City’s going down with a billion in the bank” while wavinginflatable bananas, the lattera tradition that goes back to the 1980s. It provides a reminder that City existed for 114 years before Sheikh Mansour’s investment and will continue to do so regardless of what happens in relation to potential sanctions. Many have witnessed City drop to the third tier and win the Champions League, so have experienced both ends of the spectrum already.The police flew a drone above the route the City bus planned to take into the ground, while officers walked up and down filming those in attendance as the decibels and anger grew.Every vehicle was treated with suspicion, as theories of subterfuge from City, not for the first time, were discussed. The prospect of sneaking the players and staff into the ground were gossiped about among the crowds but there was no Trojan horse. Instead the official team bus, with full livery, came up the other side of Anfield Road and around the back of the stand that bears its name.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenCity fans hold a banner reading ‘In Khaldoon we trust’ and inflatable bananas.Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty ImagesTheLiverpoolbus arrived to cheers, chants and plenty of red smoke just before 3pm. The eyes stung as the wind blew. The police presence grew closer to the anticipated arrival time on the bus.Around an hour before kick-off, after City’s coach was whisked up to the ground with its police motorcade, the visiting supporters were given their own escort across Stanley Park. The message was a defiant one, backing the chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, with verses of “We’re Man City, we’ll cheat when we want”. There was mild heckling from home fans in earshot but, like with the bus, it passed without incident. The cheering and jeering carried on while the travelling fans waited to enter the ground but it was nothing out of the ordinary for a football match between two rivals. Calmness had descended.As City walked on to the pitch for their warm-ups, they were loudly booed by the majority inside the ground, every player’s name mentioned on the public address system receiving the same treatment. City took solace in the bunch of bananas bouncing around the away end in one small corner before football finally took centre stage. Here they had the last laugh too,eventually winning 3-0to silence the home fans and maintain their lead at the top of the Premier League table. But for how long they stay at the summit or even in the league when their punishment is served, nobody knows.Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolManchester CityPremier LeagueFinancial fair playnewsShareReuse this content
